Report 
  
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of  Rajya Sabha 
  
  
            During the 195th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 267 Statutory Orders were laid 
on the Table of the House by the various Ministries/Departments.   The details of the 
Gazette Notifications in which these were published & the date of their laying on th e 
Table of the Rajya Sabha have been indicted in the enclosed Ministry wise statement 
(Annexure). 
  
2.         During the course of general scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has 
noted some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between th e date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the 
Committee’s guidelines.  In some of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal.  The 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee respect of specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows:- 
             
i.         Ministry of Commerce & Industry  
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Commerce and Industry have laid 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha the Tobacco Board (Recruitment) Regulations, 1984 
as well as the Tobacco Board (Recruitment) Regulations, 1989 just because it was not 
possible for them to confirm beyond doubt whether these regulations had been laid 

before both House of Parliament earlier as the relevant records were not traceable. 
The Committee, while it appreciates the initiative of the Ministry, but, at the same 
time, it expects them to set right their records relating to the framing and the laying 
of subordinate legislation under various Acts being administered by them at-least for 
future so that such situations are avoided. 
  
ii.         Ministry of Communication and Information Technology 
            The Committee regrets to find that out of the five notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, there has been a delay in 
case of two (sl. nos. 27 and 28 of the Annexure). The Committee expects the Ministry 
of Communication, etc. to exercise caution in such matters for future and ensure that 
the schedule as prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of subordinate 
legislation framed under various Acts of Parliament is followed meticulously from 
time to time. 
  
iii.        Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
                        The Committee regrets to note that out of 15 notifications, there has 
been a delay in laying of seven as mentioned at sl. Nos. 4,5,6,9,10, 11 and 17A of the 
Annexure. The Committee would like the Ministry of Consume r Affairs, etc. to take 
steps to avoid recurrence of such instances and ensure the compliance of the schedule 
as laid down by the Committee in the matter of laying of rules/regulations, etc. in its 
131st and 135th Reports. 
  
iv.        Ministry of Finance 
                        The Committee deeply regrets to note that for the sixth consecutive 
Session, the Ministry of Finance is coming under its particular notice due to delay in 
the laying of subordinate legislation on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. Ironic ally, the 
magnitude of the default is larger this time. The Ministry have laid 184 
rules/regulations during the 195th Session and there has been delay in case of 141 (sl. 
nos. 34, 37 39 -80, 94 -130, 135 -160, 172, 173,174, 176 -197 and 226 -227 of the 
Annexure). The Committee is even further pained to note the period by which the 
laying has been delayed which roughly averages anywhere between 8 –12 months. In 

the opinion of the Committee, calls for immediate corrective action. The Committee 
directs the Ministry of Finance to take action to prevent such lapses in the future. 
  
v.         Ministry of Home Affairs 
                        The Committee notes with regret that out of the seven notifications laid 
by the Ministry of Home Affairs during the 195 th Session, there has been a delay in 
case of five. In case of the Central Industrial Security Force Group “A” and   “B” 
Civilian Gazetted Posts Recruitment Rules, 2000, the delay is as long as of eleven 
months. The Committee would like the Ministry of Home Affairs to have a relook into 
the internal mechanism in place so as to obviate such instances for the future. 
  
vi.        Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 1 year and 2 
months on the part of Minist ry of Information & Broadcasting in laying their only 
notification, namely, the Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) 
(Audience Research Posts) Service Regulations (Sl. No. 245). 
             
The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting would 
take due care & ensure prompt compliance of the schedule prescribed by the 
Committee for the purpose. 
  
vii.       Ministry of Labour 
                        The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Labour have laid 
two notifications during the 195th Session and there has been a delay in both the cases. 
The Ministry could have laid both the notifications during the 194 th (Winter Session 
2001) of the Rajya Sabha, but they failed to do so. The Committee hopes that they 
would take necessary action and avoid such instances. 
                          
viii.      Ministry of Shipping 
The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Shipping has laid five 
notifications during the 195th Session and three out of them were delayed by a period 
ranging from 4-8 months. The Committee expects the Ministry to take necessary and 

corrective action in order to ensure that such delays do not recur and the schedule as 
prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of subordinate legislati on is 
followed, strictly.  
  
3.         Besides the above, the Committee also notes with regret the isolated cases of 
delayed laying of notifications by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (sl. 
no. 36 of the Annexure), Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs (sl. no. 249 of 
the Annexure), Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (sl. no. 258 of the 
Annexure) and Ministry of Textiles (sl. no. 258 of the Annexure). The Committee 
would like these  Ministries to take note of the time schedule which is  reproduced 
hereinafter and ensure that the same is complied with meticulously for future. The 
Committee, accordingly, reiterates its observations made in its 135th Report : 
  
 “ The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid so as t o apprise the 
Parliament of the causes of delay.   The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intention is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identifying b ottlenecks and devising remedial 
measures”.   
  
4.         The Committee impresses again upon all the Ministries/Departments to follow 
the time schedule for laying as prescribed by it in its 131st Report as reproduced below 
:- 
  
“Orders required to be laid  before the House should be laid   (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the 
date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the 
House is in Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, during 
its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication 
and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, 

before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session.  All the Ministries/Departments of  Government of India 
should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of 
the orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha.”

2.         The Committee, thereafter, took up for consideration its draft 142nd Report on 
the Statutory Orders laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha during the 195 th Session. The 
Committee noted with serious concern the delay on the part of 
Ministries/Departments in la ying of the various rules/regulations before the 

Parliament. There was a reference to the delay of 17 and 12 years, respectively in the 
laying of the Tobacco Board General Regulations, 1984 and the Tobacco Board 
Recruitment Regulations, 1989 by the Ministr y of Commerce and Industry. The 
Committee took a serious view on the Ministry’s statement that it was not possible 
for them to confirm beyond doubt whether these regulations had been laid before the 
Parliament earlier due to relevant records being not trac eable. The Committee felt 
this to be a sorry state of affairs and desired that such matters alongwith other cases 
where there has been a long delay in the laying of the rules/regulations be taken up 
with the concerned Ministries. The Committee also decided  that these 
Ministries/Departments in whose cases, there has been persistent delay in laying of 
the rules/regulations despite repeated recommendations/observations by it may also 
be identified and the   Secretary incharge of such Ministries/ Departments may  be 
asked to appear before the Committee for clarifications.  
  
3.         During the course of discussion on the draft Report, there was also a mention 
about the delay in framing of the subordinate legislation under various Acts of 
Parliament. A view was expressed that there should be some definite criteria for 
ascertaining whether there has been a delay in framing of the rules/ regulations or 
not. While it was appreciated that the process of framing of subordinate legislations 
was t ime consuming and the time required for the purpose may vary from one 
legislation to another, but, there was a suggestion that the Ministries/Departments 
may also be required to indicate in the memorandum of delegated legislation 
appended to the Bill, whic h gives the areas which are contemplated to be covered 
through subordinate legislation, the approximate time which would be required for 
framing the subordinate legislation and any delay beyond this time limit could be 
pursued by the Committee as a case of  delay. The Committee desired this aspect to 
be examined. The Committee also desired the Secretariat to examine the cases where 
there has been an unusual delay in framing of the rules/regulations for its 
consideration. The draft 142nd Report was, thereafter, adopted.

NEW DELHI 
August 12, 2002 
A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN 
Chairman 
 Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
 Rajya Sabha 
  

  
 
REPORT 
  
I 
  
The Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965 
  
            The Committee examined the Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965 
and certain points were referred to the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department 
of Commerce) on June 21, 1999 for their comments/clarifications.  The subject matter 
was taken up for discussion with the representatives of the Coffee Board and the 
Ministry of Commerce & Industry at Bangalore on June 28, 1999.  The points referred 
and the comments/clarifications of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry alongwith the 
Committee’s observation are reproduced below. 
  
1.         Point referred 
  
Whether these Rules have been laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha; if so, the details 
thereof, if not the reasons therefore? 
  
            Ministry’s Comments: 
  
These Rules would definitely have been laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.  However, 
since these Rules were framed 34 years ago, it is very difficult to locate records to 
authenticate our claim. 
            Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee expressed its concern over the non-availability of dates of laying of the 
rules on the Table of the Houses of Parliament.  The representatives assured to revert 
back to Committee on the issue at their earliest. 
  
2.         Point  referred 
Rule 2(1)(g) 
  
            “Family means” 
  
In the case of a male subscriber, the wife or wives and children of  a  subscriber  and 
the  widow, or widows, and  
children of the deceased son of a subscriber:  provided that if a subscriber proves that 
his wife has been judicially separated from him or has ceased under the customary law 
of the community to which  she belongs to be entitled  
to maintenance she shall henceforth be deemed to be no longer a member of the 
subscriber’s family in matter to which these rules relate unless the subscriber 
subsequently intimates in writing to the Accounts Officer that she shall continue to be so 
regarded; 
  
In the case of female subscriber, the husband and children of a subscriber and the 
widow or widows and children of a deceased son of a subscriber: provided that if a 
subscriber by notice in writing to the Accounts Officer expresses her desire to exclude 
her husband from her family, the husband shall henceforth be deemed to be no longer a 

member of the subscriber’s family in matter to which these rules relate unless the 
subscriber subsequently cancels such notice in writing: 
  
            Provisions in sub-clauses (i) & (ii) of clause (g) of sub-rules (1) of Rule 2 
prescribe different procedures in case of male and female employees of the Coffee 
Board for exclusion of spouse from the subscribers family. 
  
What is the justification for prescribing different procedures; whether Government 
have any objections in prescribing a uniform procedure for both male and female 
employees? 
 Ministry’s Comments 
  
            Since Coffee Board has adopted the Central Government General Provident 
Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960 for the employees of the Coffee Board, the definition 
of family will be the same as the Central Government Employees.  Ministry of 
Commerce or Coffee Board are not competent to make any change  in the definition of 
family as these are based on  the  rules  framed  by  the   Government   of  India  in  the  
Department of Personnel which are applicable to all Central Government Employees. 
  
Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee noted the reply. 
  
3.         Point referred 
            Rule 8(1) 
  
                        Conditions of subscriptions  
                         
“A subscriber shall subscribe monthly to the Fund except during  the period when he is 
under suspension;  
Provided that a subscriber may at his option, not subscribe during any period of leave, 
other than leave on average pay or earned leave of less than one month or 30 days 
duration, as the case may be;”   
  
As per the above proviso a subscriber may not subscribe to the Fund if he is on earned 
leave of a duration of more than 30 days or on some other leave.  What is the 
justification of keeping such a provision?  There is no such provision in the General 
Provident Fund rules applicable to Central Government Employees. 
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            Though the provision was incorporated in the Coffee Board General Provident 
Fund Rules, 1965, in practice these provisions are not given effect to. 
  
            In fact Rule 28 of the Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965, very 
clearly states that: 
  
“Notwithstanding the above provision, if the Central Government notify any change in 
the rate of subscription or modify  the  rules  and  procedures relating to advances  
and withdrawals in the General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960, such 
change shall be made applicable to the servant of the Board also.” 
  

            With the aid of this enabling provision in the CBGPF Rules, 1965, the Board has 
been adopting all the changes made in the   Central PF Rules through the issue of 
relevant circulars.   The Board strictly follows the provisions of the General Provident 
Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960. 
  
            Committee’s Observations 
  
The Committee was not satisfied with the Ministry’s reply and observed that when the 
proviso to Rule 8(1) has not been given effect to there is no justification for having such 
a provision in the Rule.  This proviso, therefore, should have been omitted from the 
Rules. 
  
4.         Point referred 
            Rule 9(1)(b) 
  
            Rates of subscription 
             
“The amount of subscription shall be fixed by the subscriber himself, subject to the 
following conditions, namely- 
  
It may be any sum, so expressed not less than 6 per cent of his emoluments and not 
more than his total emoluments; 
  
Provided that in the case of a subscriber who has previously been subscribing to the 
Board’s Contributory Provident Fund at the higher rate of 8 1/3  per cent, it may by 
any sum, so expressed, not less than 8 1/3 per cent, of his emoluments and not more 
than his total emoluments; 
  
Provided further that in case of class IV employees the minimum rate of subscription 
shall be Rs.4/- a month in the case of those drawing a pay of less than Rs.75/- a month 
and Rs.5/- a month in the case of others.” 
  
            The minimum amounts mentioned in the second proviso for class IV and other 
employees of the Board is very less.  Perhaps, these figures are based upon very old pay 
scale.  Whether the Ministry would inform when these limits were fixed; whether these 
limits are not due for revision and if so, by when these would be revised? 
             
            Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            It is submitted that the minimum subscription towards PF contribution by the 
Board employees has been fixed at the rate of 6% of the basic pay drawn by the 
respective officer/officials.  This procedure/practice has been in force in accordance 
with the General Provident Fund Rules and in accordance with the Rules 28 of Coffee 
Board General Provident Fund Rules. 
  
            Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee was not satisfied with the reply and observed that when the second 
proviso to Rule 9(1) had not been given effect to there was no justification for having 
such a provision in the Rule.  This proviso, therefore, should be omitted from the Rules. 
  
5.         Point referred 

        Rule 9(4) 
             
Rates of subscription 
  
                        XXX                            XXX                   XXX                          
                        XXX                            XXX                   XXX                                     XXX       
         XXX                    XXX                             
                         
“The amount of subscription so fixed may by enhanced or reduced once at any time 
during the course of a year;” 
                         
            According to the rule the amount of subscription may be enhanced or reduced 
once at any time during the course of a year. 
  
As per Rule 9(4) of the General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rules, 1960, the 
amount of subscription once fixed can be enhanced twice during the course of the 
year.  Whether there is any objection to amend the rule accordingly? 
  
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            The Board is permitting the subscribers to enhance the subscription towards PF 
twice in a financial year and once in a year of reduction of  subscription.  The necessary 
modifications have not been formally included in the CBGPF Rules, 1965, only because 
the Rules have not been re-printed.  The subscription will never be allowed below 6% of 
the basis pay of the respective employees. 
  
            Committee’s Observation 
  
            The Committee was not satisfied with the reply and observed that necessary 
formal modifications in the Coffee Board rules have to be carried out to allow the 
subscribers to enhance the subscription towards Provident Fund twice in a year.  The 
Committee further observed that mere reprinting of these rules was not the solution. 
  
6.         Point referred 
Rule 13(1)(b) 
  
Advance from the Fund  
  
The Chairman or any other officer of the Board, not below the rank of an Assistant 
Coffee Marketing Officer, authorised by the Chairman, may sanction the payment to 
any subscriber if an advance consisting of a sum of whole rupees and  not exceeding 
in  amount  three months pay or  
half the amount standing to his credit in the Fund whichever is less, for one or more of 
the following purposes: 
  
XXX                XXX                  XXX                                                  
to meet the cost of higher education, including where necessary, the travelling expenses 
of the subscriber or any person actually dependent on him in the following cases, 
namely. 
  
(i)         for education outside India for an academic, technical, professional or 
vocational course beyond the High School stage: and 

  
for any medical, engineering or the technical or specialised   courses in India beyond the 
High School stage provide that the course of study is for not less than  three years. 
  
            What is the objective for prescribing that a course of study should not be of less 
than three years. Whether the Ministry have any objection to delete the words 
“provided that the course of study is not less than three years” as many of the technical 
courses are expensive and are of lesser duration.  (Question also applies to rule 
16(1)(a)). 
  
            Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            The provision of “not less than three years” is being followed as per Rule 12 (b) 
(ii) of the Central GPF Rules which also prescribes this minimum requirement of 
time.  For all purposes, the Board follows only the Central PF Rule.  The Coffee Board 
does not have the authority to alter this, as this is a decision,  which can be taken only 
by the Union Government. 
             
            This answer holds good for Rule 16(1)(a) also. 
             
            Committee’s Observation 
  
The Committee noted the reply 
  
Point referred 
Rule 16 
  
Withdrawals from the Fund 
  
“Subject to conditions specified herein, withdrawals may be sanctioned by the chairman 
at any time after the completion of twenty years of service (including broken periods of 
service, if any) of a subscriber or within ten years before the date of retirement on 
superannuating, whichever is earlier, from the amount standing for his credit in the 
fund, for one or more of the following purposes, namely”- 
  
            For the Central Government Employees’ there has been a modification in the 
condition for withdrawal wherein they have been allowed to withdraw after completing 
15 years of service.  Coffee Board is still carrying the condition of 20 years of service in 
this regard.  What is the justification that a provision which is for the benefit of the 
Employees and which has been introduced in the Central Government in year 1995 has 
not been incorporated in these regulation so far? 
  
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            From 1995 and onwards withdrawal from the respective PF accounts are being 
allowed to those employees who have completed 15 years service.   Prior to 1995, final 
withdrawal used to be allowed to such of the employees who had completed 20 years 
service. 
             
            Committee’s Observation 
             

            The Committee observed that although the Coffee is extending all the benefit 
that are available in the General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rules applicable to 
the Central Government Employees yet they have not amended these  rules for the 
purpose.  The Committee desired that corresponding amendments be made in the rules. 
  
Point referred 
  
            In the case of GPF Rules applicable to Central Government Employees there has 
been relaxation in the grant of advances as well as withdrawal for purpose of various 
consumers durables.  Whether the Ministry have taken any action for incorporating 
similar provisions in these regulations if so, the details thereof, if not the reasons 
therefore? 
  
Ministry’s Comments: 
  
            PF advance/withdrawals are allowed to purchase consumer durables in 
accordance with the directions of the Government. 
  
            Committee’s Observation 
  
            The Committee observed in general that in relation to several matters, the Coffee 
Board has been implementing the existing provisions of the General Provident Fund 
Rules applicable in Government of India without formal amendments in their 
rules.  The Committee did not approve this dispensation and observed that Coffee 
Board should follow the Central Government rules by making consequent changes in 
their rules  which would be a proper course of action. 
  
The Relevant extracts from the study note (Annexure-I) on the Committee’s visit to 
Bangalore etc., from June 27 to July 3, 1999 were forwarded to the Ministry on 
September 21, 1999 for necessary action.  The Ministry vide their O. M. dated 
November 19, 1999 informed that Coffee Board  has  accepted the 
Committee’s  suggestion for inserting a  
new clause in the Coffee Rules 1955 to the effect that employee of Board shall be 
governed by General Provident Fund (Central Service) Rule 1960 instead of having a 
separate set of rules and the process of making necessary amendment to the Coffee 
Rules for inserting a new clause had been initiated by the Ministry. 
  
3.         Thereafter, the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Department of Commerce 
vide their O. M. dated July 24, 2000 intimated as under. 
  
                        XXX                         XXX                           XXX                             
  
“The proposal for making necessary amendment to the Coffee Rules, 1955 for inserting 
a new clause was taken up with the Legislative Department However, Legislative 
Department is not agreeable to the proposal and has advised this Department for 
updating the existing Coffee Board’s General Provident Fund Rules, 
1965.  Accordingly, the process for amending the existing GPF Rules of the Board is 
under way.” 
  
4.         After some reminders and interim replies, the Ministry of Commerce & Industry 
vide their O. M. dated April 17, 2001 forwarded a copy of the Coffee Board General 

Provident Fund (Amendment) Rules, 2001(Annexure-II) carrying out the amendment in 
the rules as per the Committee’s suggestion. 
5.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have carried out 
necessary amendment in the rules in pursuance to the deliberations with the latter. The 
Committee notes Ministry’s comments on Rule 2(1)(g) regarding definition of the term 
“family” and on rule 13(1)(b) regarding withdrawal of advance from Fund.  As regards 
the date of laying of the rules on the Table of the House the Committee notes with regret 
that the Ministry have failed to gather the desired information.  The Ministry should 
strive for a better  record management system in order to avoid such instances.   
The Committee, however, notes that the Ministry have laid the rules again on the 20th 
March, 2001 in order to cover up the prevailing uncertainty.  The Committee is also 
satisfied to note that the Ministry have agreed to its suggestions and, accordingly, 
notified amendments in Rules 8(1) regarding conditions and rate of subscriptions, in 
Rule 9(1)(b) regarding rates of subscription by omitting its second proviso, in Rule 9(4) 
regarding enhancement and reduction in the amount of subscription during a calendar 
year, in Rule-16 regarding withdrawal from the Fund and the purposes for which 
withdrawal is allowed by making them consistent with the corresponding provisions of 
the GPF Rules applied to Central Government employees.

II 
  
The Merchant Shipping (Management of Safe Operation of Ships) Rules, 2000 
             
            The Merchant Shipping (Management for the Safe Operation of Ships) Rules, 
2000 framed under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 were examined and certain points 
were referred to the Ministry of Shipping for their comments/clarifications on 
December 22, 2000. The Ministry vide their communication dated February 6, 2001 had 
furnished their comments. The points referred to the Ministry and the 
comments/clarifications received thereon are as under:  
  
Point referred. 
  
The Rules have been framed under Section 457 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 
1958.  What are the reasons that Government did not have any set of rules on the 
subject for over 4 decades & in what manner Government had been regulating this area 
of activity; what factors necessitated Government to frame the said Rules, now? 
  
            Ministry’s reply 
  
            Safe operation of ships and pollution prevention (International Safety 
Management Code) vide IMO Resolution No. A 741(18) dated May 1994 was made 
mandatory by Chapter IX of SOLAS  Convention, and has come into force from 1st July 
1998 depending on the type and tonnage of ships.  This code applies to passenger ships, 
tankers, gas carriers and bulk carriers and high speed crafts not later than1st July 
1998.  
  
            This code shall apply to other cargo ships and mobile offshore crafts not later 
than 1st July 2002.  The purpose of this Code is to provide international standard for the 
safe management and operation of ships and for pollution prevention.  These aspects 
are already covered under parts IX & XIA of the Merchant Shipping Act and 
various  Certificates  were prescribed  for  various activities.   The same activities are 
now proposed to be conducted in a different form to enhance better management.

In these  rules, unless the context otherwise requires:- 
  
(j) “Designated person”  means a person ashore with direct access to the highest level of 
management charged with the responsibility and the authority to monitor the safety and 
pollution aspects of the operation of each ship. 
  
“Safety Management Certificate” means a Certificate issued by Director General of 
Shipping or any officer authorised by him in this behalf to a ship which signifies that the

Management System.

designation/qualification of the designated person. What are the functions assigned to 
the ‘Designated person’ and under what provisions  of Act/Rules these have been 
enumerated.

provisions of these rules.  So much so that the words ‘Designated Person’ have not been 
used anywhere else but in the definition. What may the reasons be for defining a term 
which has not been used in the provisions of the rules.   
  
(ii) In Sub rule (u) the Director General of Shipping has been 
authorized  to  delegate  the  power  to  issue  the  ‘Safety  Management Certificate’  to

Ministry’s reply 
  
Rule 2 (j) it is agreed that the designated person has not been reflected anywhere in the

Whether the recruitment rules contemplated under regulation 28(8) for the purpose of 
filling up posts under the Authority have been notified with the approval of the Central 
Government; if so, the details thereof. 
  
Comments 
  
            The draft Recruitment rules of APEDA was sent to the Legislative Department 
on 16th June 2000 for vetting.  The same has been received from that Department on 
12th September 2000 with the suggestion for incorporating certain modifications.  After 
examination of the suggestions of the Legislative Department, it will be sent to that 
Department for vetting.  After the legislative Department had vetted, immediate action 
will be taken to notify the Rules and then laid on the Table of both the Houses of 
Parliament. 
  
Committee’s observations 
  
Committee noted the reply 
Point referred 
  
Regulation 28(9)(b) 
  
All appointments to the post carrying the scale of pay, the maximum of which is not less 
than Rs. 13,500/- shall be made by the Central Government as per the instructions 
issued in this behalf from time to  time either through deputation of suitable officer 
from Central/State Governments  or through direct recruitment. 
  
Whether the recruitment rules contemplated under regulation 28(8) cover filling up of 
Group ‘A’ posts and, if so, what is the justification for having a separate provision 
prescribing the manner in which Group ‘A’ posts in the Authority may be filled up; 
what is the justification for giving final authority to the Central Government for 
deciding the manner in which any Group ‘A’ posts in the Authority may be filled up? 
Comments 
  
The Recruitment Rules to be notified will cover filling up of Group ‘A’ posts also.  The 
provision made in the Regulation is of general nature and the detailed method of 
recruitment’s, scales of pay, qualifications, etc. have been prescribed in the proposed 
Recruitment Rules. 
  
Section 32 sub-section (2)(d) and Section 33 sub-section (2)(b) of the Agricultural and 
Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985 vests the Central 
Government with such Authority. 
             
            Committee’s observations 

  
Committee noted the reply 
  
Point referred 
  
Regulation 28(9)(f) 
  
The Authority may contract services, as deemed fit.  No contract 
appointments   of   more   than 6 months   duration and/or  having basic monthly 
remuneration of Rs. 1800/-or more shall be made without prior approval of the Central 
Government. 
  
            Whether the functional requirements of the Authority are being met 
satisfactorily in view of the powers conferred upon it to allow contract appointments on 
remuneration up to Rs.1800/-per month? Secondly,  what  does  the words ‘basic 
monthly remuneration”  
signify; generally, remuneration is the total payment receivable by a person for services 
rendered and it is not clear what objective is sought to be achieved for qualifying 
remuneration by using the word ‘basic’? Should, the limits ofremuneration up to which 
contract appointments could be given be not definite? 
  
Comments 
  
The amount of Rs.1800/-mentioned in Regulation 28(9)(f) has since been amended to be 
Rs. 6000/- vide Notification No. APEDA/SEC/GEN/30 dated 5th May 2000.  The amount 
of Rs.6000/- mentioned here is the limit of total remuneration upto which contract 
appointments could be made by the Authority.  The amount of Rs.6000/- is the total 
payment receivable by a person for services rendered.  The word ‘basic’ could be 
deleted. 
  
Committee’s observations 
  
The Committee noted that under Regulation 28(9)(f) the Ministry have agreed to delete 
the word ‘basic’ as observed by the Committee. 
  
The Committee  notes the comments of the Ministry on point no. 1,2,6,9, & 10. The 
Committee is satisfied that the Ministry have agreed to its suggestions on regulations 7 
(point-3) for raising minimum strength of the quorum from 8 to 10 Members, 
regulation 10 and 26 (point-4) for modifying the existing provision of “second or casting 
vote” available to the Chairman or the presiding Officer, regulation-11(2) (point-5) for 
deleting the word “effectual” which was a printing mistake, Regulation 15(2) (point-7) 
for defining the words “of a policy nature”, regulation-16 (point-8) for providing a time 
limit within which the Authority can review the decision of the Committee and 
regulation-28(9) (F) (point-11) by substituting the words “basic monthly remuneration” 
with  the words “monthly remuneration”.  
  
The Committee recommends to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to carry out 
the above amendments in the regulations expeditiously under intimation to it. 
 
  
IV 
  

Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust Employees (Pay and Allowances)     Regulation, 1997-
Implementation of 79th Report of the Committee 
  
The Committee had examined the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust Employees (Pay and 
Allowances)Regulations, 1997 and made certain observations/recommendations as 
contained in its 126th Report which was presented to the House on December 23, 
1999.  The recommendations made by the Committee are as follows: 
  
“The Committee expresses satisfaction that the Ministry of Surface Transport had 
agreed to amend regulations 4, 19(1) and 24 as per its suggestions.  As regards 
regulation 2(19) the Committee decided that the regulation may be retained in its 
existing form.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Surface Transport will notify 
the amendments to regulation 4, 19(1) and 24 expeditiously under intimation to it.” 
  
The extracts from the Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Shipping (then 
Ministry of Surface Transport) on January 28, 2000 for implementation.  The Ministry 
of Shipping vide their O.M. dated 28.7.2000  forwarded a copy  of the notification No. 
G.S.R. 724 (E) dated 27.10.1999 containing the amendment in respect of Regulation  4 
and 19(1).   The  proposal to amend the regulation 24 was, however, stated to be  under 
process.  
After a couple of reminders the Ministry of Shipping vide their O.M. dated 27.6.2001 
forwarded a copy of the notification No. G.S.R. 443 (E) dated 21.6. 2001 containing 
amendment to the regulation 24 also. 
  
4.         The Committee expresses its satisfaction that the Ministry have amended 
regulation 4 (1) (a) (i) by deleting the words, “or rupees twenty five only, whichever is 
more”, regulation 19 by deleting sub-regulation 2 and its proviso regarding crediting of 
fee and honorarium to the General Account of Port  and  regulation 24 by rewording 
the provisions of sub-regulation 2(ii). 
 
SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS 
  
I 
  
The Coffee Board General Provident Fund Rules, 1965 
  
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have carried out 
necessary amendment in the rules in pursuance to the deliberations with the latter. The 
Committee notes Ministry’s comments on Rule 2(1)(g) regarding definition of the term 
“family” and on rule 13(1)(b) regarding withdrawal of advance from Fund.  As regards 
the date of laying of the rules on the Table of the House the Committee notes with regret

regarding enhancement and reduction in the amount of subscription during a calendar

withdrawal is allowed by making them consistent with the corresponding provisions of 
the GPF Rules applied to Central Government employees.   

II 
  
The Merchant Shipping (Management of Safe Operation of Ships) Rules, 2000 
  
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Shipping have agreed 
to take action as follows based upon the suggestions on  Committee’s behalf: 
  
 Prescribing minimum level of the Officers for issuing   Safety Management Certificate 
on behalf of the Central Government of India  by amending rule  2(u) ;  
  
amending rule 3(1)  by re-writing the para so as to provide that the system is a part of

indicating mandatory rules and regulations mentioned in rule 3(b)(i) ;  
  
deleting the words “International Safety Management” in rule 3(1)(b)(ii) so as to 
provide that applicable codes, guidelines, and standards recommended by the 
Organization, Central Government, Classification Societies and Maritime industry 
organizations are taken into account”, and; 
  
joining sub rule (a) of rule 4 with rule 4.  
  
             The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Shipping would carry out the above 
amendments  expeditiously  with intimation to it. 
  
III 
  
The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority 
Regulations, 1999 
  
The Committee  notes the comments of the Ministry on point no. 1,2,6,9, & 10. The 
Committee is satisfied that the Ministry have agreed to its suggestions on regulations 7 
(point-3) for raising minimum strength of the quorum from 8 to 10 Members, 
regulation 10 and 26 (point-4) for modifying the existing provision of “second or casting 
vote” available to the Chairman or the presiding Officer, regulation-11(2) (point-5) for

nature”, regulation-16 (point-8) for providing a time limit within which the Authority 
can review the decision of the Committee and regulation-28(9) (F) (point-11) by 
substituting the words “basic monthly remuneration” with  the words “monthly

The Committee recommends to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to carry out 
the above amendments in the regulations expeditiously under intimation to it. 
  
IV

INTRODUCTION 
  
      I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been authorized 
by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Hu ndred 
and Forty Fifth  Report of the Committee. 
. 
1.2  The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held 
on  December  9, 2002 
  
1.3  The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the Table of the Rajya 
Sabha during its 196th session have been perused by the Committee in the light of 
the provisions of the Acts under which these were framed and also with a view to 
seeing whether these have been laid within the prescribed time -frame and 
properly.  The Committee’s observations/ recommendations are contained in the 
report that follows.  
  
  
NEW DELHI 
December 9, 2002 
A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN 
Chairman 
 Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
Rajya Sabha 
  
  
 
 Report 
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of  Rajya Sabha 
  
      During the 196 th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 78 Statutory Orders were laid on the 
Table of the House by the various Ministries/Departments.   The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were published and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise statement placed at Annexure. 
  
2.   During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Comm ittee has noted some cases 
where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of notification of the Order 
and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in 
cases where notifications have not been laid as pe r the Committee’s guidelines.  In some 
of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal.   The observations/ recommendations of 
the Committee in respect of specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: - 
  

I     Ministry of Commerce & Industry  
      The Committee notes that out of the five notifications laid by the Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry, there has been a delay in two cases (sl. nos. 6 and 7 
)  of  the  Annexure. The Ministry have also not enclosed the delay statement giving the 
reasons for  the delay in laying. The Committee expects the Ministry of Commerce & 
Industry to exercise caution in such matters and ensure that the   schedule as prescribed 
by the Committee in the matter of laying of Subordinate Legislation framed under 
various Acts of Parliament is followed meticulously in future . 
  
II    Ministry of Finance & Company Affairs 
  
      The Committee is unhappy over the fact that for the seventh consecutive session, 
the  Ministry  of Finance and Company Affairs are  
coming under its particular notice on account of delay in the laying of Subordinate 
Legislation on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. The Ministry have laid 30 rules/regulations 
during the 196 th Session and there has been delay in case of 27 ranging from 1 year 5 
months to 3 months as shown in the Annexure and in none of the cases, delay statement 
has been appended.  The Committee   recommends that the Ministry of Finance and 
Company Affairs  should take immediate corrective action and ensure that henceforth 
the subordinate legislation is laid before the Parliament on time. 
  
III  Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
      The Committee notes with regret that out of the eleven notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Home Affairs during the 196 th Session, there has been delay in case  of four 
(sl. nos. 54 to 56 and 58).   The Committee would like the Ministry to streamline its 
procedures so as to obviate such instances in future.  
  
IV  Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
  
      The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of five months in laying 
two of the notifications (sl. nos. 61 and 63) and no delay statement was sent 
therewith.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting 
would take adequate steps to ensure compliance with the time sche dule as laid down by 
the Committee for the laying of Subordinate Legislation. 
  
V    Ministry of Law and Justice  
      The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of seven months on the 
part of the Ministry  of Law  and Justice  in laying   
their only   notification (sl. no. 64)   and  no  delay  statement  has been enclosed. The 
Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and ensure compliance 
with the time schedule for laying of notifications in future.  
             
VI  Ministry of Urban Development & Poverty Alleviation 
  
      The Committee regrets to note that out of two notifications laid during the 196 th 
Session, one has been delayed by four months.   The Committee expects the Ministry to 
take necessary corrective action in order to ensure that such delays do not recur and the 
schedule as prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of Subordinate 
Legislation is followed strictly. 
  

3.   The Committee also notes with regret the delayed laying of notification at s l. No. 10 
of the Annexure by the Ministry of Civil Aviation by four months and that too without 
any delay statement.   
  
4.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate 
steps to avoid delay in laying of subordinate legisl ation. The Committee, accordingly, 
wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones as enumerated above the following recommendations as 
contained in its 131 st Report wherein a time sched ule for the laying of subordinate 
legislation has been prescribed as follows: 
  
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  (i) if the House is not 
in Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication of the 
Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the 
publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between 
the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 
clear days, before the expiry of   the  Session immediately following the said 
Session.   
All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply 
with this schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued under various Acts 
of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
  
 5.  The Committee also reiterates its following observations made in its 135 th Report 
regarding appending of delay statement where there has been delay in the laying: 
  
“ The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case 
there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned 
Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
notifications being laid so as to apprise the Parliament of the causes of delay.  The 
Committee desires all Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the 
intention is that through the process of formulation of a delay st atement the 
Ministry is able to introspect, identifying bottlenecks and devising remedial 
measures”.

Seventh Meeting 
  
      The Committee met at 3.30 p.m. on Monday,   the 9th December, 2002 in Room No.  
126-C (Chairman’s Room) Third Floor, Parliament House, New Delhi. 
                         
MEMBERS PRESENT 
  
      1.   Shri A. Vijayaraghavan    Chairman                       
            2.   Dr. A.R. Kidwai 
            3.   Shri B.P. Singhal 
            4.   Shri Ravula Chandra Sekhar Reddy 
            5.   Shri Drupad Borgohain 
SECRETARIAT 
  
      1.   Shri N.C. Joshi, Joint Secretary 
2.      Shri Deepak Goyal, Deputy Secretary 
3.    Shri Ram Behari Gupta, Under Secretary 
4.   Shri Arun Sharma, Committee Officer 
  
2.       The Committee took up for consideration its draft 145 th Report on the Statutory 
Orders laid on the table of the Rajya Sabha during the 196 th Session.  While considering 
the Report, the Committee also had a look into the delay in the laying of Statutory Orders 
by the various Ministries/Departments during the previous five to six Sessions and it 
noted that the delay in laying had been quite persistent.   The Committee further noted 
that in majority of such cases of delay, the Ministries/ Departments had even failed to 
append a delay statement explaining the reasons for delay in the laying of 
the  notifications despite Committees’ specific  and  clear recommendations to that effect  
in its 131 st Report which had been reiterated a number of times.  The Committee, 
accordingly, decided to hear the representatives   of the Ministries of Finance and 
Company Affairs and Home Affairs on the question of persistent delay in the laying of 
their notifications. 
  
3.   The Committee, thereafter, adopted its draft 145th Report and decided to present 
it to the House on the 12th December, 2002.  The Committee authorized the Chairman 
and in his absence Shri B.P.Singhal and Shri Ravula Chandra Sekar Reddy MPs to 
present the Report. 
  
4.   The Committee also decided to meet again at 3.00 p.m. on the 9th January, 2003. 
  
5.  The meeting then adjourned at 4.30  p.m.

            I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been 
authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this 
Hundred and Forty Sixth Report of the Committee. 
. 
The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on  31.03.2003. 
  
1.3       The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha during its 197th session have been perused by the Committee in the light of 
the provisions of the Acts under which these were framed and also with a view to seeing 
whether these have been laid within the prescribed time-frame and properly.  The 
Committee’s observations/recommendations are contained in the report that follows.  
   
  

new delhi 
March 31,2003 
A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN  
Chairman 
 Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
 Rajya Sabha 
  
 
Report 
  
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of  Rajya Sabha 
  
            During the 197th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 233 Statutory Orders were laid on 
the Table of the House by various Ministries/Departments.  The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were published and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise statement placed at 
Annexure. 
  
2.         During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted some 
cases where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of notification of 
the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of 
delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the Committee’s guidelines 
and whether such notifications were accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons 
for delay in laying.  In some of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal.  The 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee in respect of specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows: - 
I           Ministry of Commerce & Industry: 
            The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
have delayed the laying of 3 of their notifications (sl. nos. 6 to 8 of the Annexure) out of 
the 8 notifications laid by them during the Session. Appropriately, notification at sl. no. 
8 could have been laid during the Budget (195th) Session of 2002 and the notifications at 
sl. nos. 6 and 7 during the Monsoon (196th) Session. The Ministry have also failed to 
append the delay statement along with these 3 notifications as has been recommended 
by the Committee. There had been cases of delay in laying by this Ministry during the 
196th and 197th Sessions also in pursuance to which the Committee had recommended 
the Ministry to take suitable remedial action. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Commerce & Industry would take prompt remedial action and comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of subordinate legislation. 

  
II         Ministry of  Communication & Information Technology: 
             
The Committee regrets to note that out of the 5 notifications laid by this Ministry, there 
has been an inordinate delay of one year and nine months in case of notification at sl. 
no. 15 and 6 months in case of notification at sl. no. 17. The Ministry have even failed to 
append the delay statement in the former case where the delay has been very large. The 
Committee has come across some instances of delay in case of this Ministry in the past 
sessions also like in the 191st, 194th and 196th Sessions of the Rajya Sabha. The 
Committee would like the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology to 
take necessary corrective measures so as to ensure the compliance of the Committee’s 
recommendations in the matter of laying of subordinate legislation. 
  
III        Ministry of Environment & Forests: 
  
The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Environment & Forests did not 
comply with the schedule for laying in case of 10 out of 12 notifications laid during the 
197th Session and the delay ranging from 1 year to 4 years 4 months as shown in the 
Annexure (sl. nos. 24 to 33).  The Committee suggests that the Ministry of Environment 
& Forests should take immediate corrective action and ensure that henceforth the 
Subordinate Legislation is laid before the Parliament on time. 
  
IV        Ministry of Finance & Company Affairs: 
  
            The Committee is extremely unhappy to note that the Ministry of Finance and 
Company Affairs have not complied with the schedule for laying of the notifications as 
prescribed by the Committee in its 131st Report for the eighth consecutive session of the 
Rajya Sabha. The Ministry have laid 129 rules/regulations during the 197th Session and 
there has been delay in case of 77 ranging from 4 months to 12 months as shown in the 
Annexure and delay statement has been appended only in 8 cases.  
            The Committee, being concerned over the persistent delay in the laying of 
Subordinate Legislation by the Ministry of Finance eversince it had started examining 
this aspect from the 191st Session onwards on a regular basis, heard the Secretary, 
Ministry of Finance along with the Secretaries of different Departments under the 
Ministry on the question of non-compliance of the schedule as laid down by the 
Committee in this behalf on the 9th January 2003. During the course of the oral 
evidence, the Finance Secretary, while admitting delay in laying, assured the Committee 
that they were taking appropriate remedial action in order to avoid such delays for 
future. The Committee hopes that there would be concerted efforts on the part of 

Ministry would help to eliminate such instances of delay in laying of Subordinate 
Legislation in future.  
  
V         Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: 
  
            The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 5 notifications laid (sl. nos. 
164-168), there has been a delay of 4 months in laying of two notifications and no delay 
statement has been annexed therewith.  There were instances of delay in a number of 
cases during the 192nd and 194th to 196th Sessions also. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare would take adequate steps to ensure compliance 
with the time schedule as laid down by the Committee for the laying of Subordinate 
Legislation in future. 
  
VI        Ministry of Home Affairs: 
  
            The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 4 months and 7 
months in case of laying two notifications (sl. nos. 171 and 174) out of 6 notifications 
laid.  The delay statement was enclosed only in one case (Sl No. 174). There were 
instances of delay in a number of cases during the 192nd and 194th to 196th Sessions also. 
Keeping in view the fact that there had been delay in laying in a fairly large number of 
cases from the 191st Session onwards of the Rajya Sabha eversince the Committee have 
taken up such a scrutiny on a regular basis, the Committee heard the oral evidence of 
the Secretary, Home Affairs on the 9th January 2003. During the course of the oral 
evidence, the Committee was assured that the Ministry were taking suitable action to 
avoid recurrence of such delays in future. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Home Affairs would be able to keep to their promise.  
  
VII          Ministry of Human Resource Development: 
  
            The Committee notes with regret that there is a delay in laying in all the three 
notifications laid by the Ministry of Human Resource Development during the 197th 
Session (sl nos. 175 to 177). There had been instances of delay in laying in a number of 
cases during the 191st and 194th to 196th Sessions also. The Committee would like the 
Ministry to streamline their procedures so as to obviate such instances in future. 
  
VIII     Ministry of Information & Broadcasting :  

  
            The Committee is distressed to note that out of the 12 notifications laid during 
the 197th Session, 10 have been delayed by period ranging from 6 to 7 months.  Further, 
delay statement has been enclosed only with four notifications  (sl. nos. 181, 183, 187 & 
188).  The Committee expects that the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting would 
take appropriate steps to comply with time schedule laid by the Committee for the 
laying of Subordinate Legislation. 
  
IX        Ministry of Labour: 
  
            The Committee regrets to note that out of the 5 notifications laid by the Ministry, 
there has been delay in 2 cases (sl. nos. 193 & 194) by 5 and 6 months, respectively, and 
no delay statement has been appended. There were instances of delay in a considerable 
number of cases during the 191st, 192nd, 194th and 196th sessions also.  The Committee 
recommends the Ministry to stick to the time schedule as recommended by the 
Committee in its 135th Report in laying the   Subordinate Legislation before the 
Parliament. 
  
X         Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions:  
  
             The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel,  Public 
Grievances and Pensions have  laid 16 rules/regulations  during the 197th Session out of 
which 12 have been delayed by period ranging from 7 months to 19 months. There were 
instances of delay during the 191st to 193rd Sessions also. The Committee expects the 
Ministry to be cautious in such matters and ensure compliance with time schedule for 
laying the notifications in future. 
  
XI        Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas: 
  
            The Committee notes that two notifications laid by the Ministry of Petroleum  & 
Natural   Gas have been delayed by 9 to 10 months (sl. nos. 213 & 214).  The Ministry 
have also not enclosed the delay statement giving the reasons for the delay in 
laying.  The Committee expects the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas to exercise 
caution in such matters and ensure that the schedule as prescribed by the Committee in 
the matter of laying of Subordinate Legislation framed under various Acts of 
Parliament is followed meticulously in future. 
  

XII  Ministry of Power: 
  
            The Committee regrets to note the Ministry of Power have laid 3 notifications 
during the 197th Session out of which 2 have been delayed by 4 to 5 months (sl. nos. 215 
and 216).  The Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and 
ensure compliance with time schedule for laying the rules/regulations in future. 
  
XIII  Ministry of Shipping:   
  
            The Committee notes that there has been an extreme delay of 2 years and 7 
months on the part of the Ministry in laying 2 of its notifications (sl nos. 230 & 
231).  There were instances of delay in a  
  
number of cases during the 194th and 196th Sessions also. The Committee would like the 
Ministry of Shipping to take remedial measure to prevent recurrence of such action and 
also ensure that henceforth the Subordinate Legislation is laid before the Parliament on 
time. 
  
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate 
steps to avoid delay in laying of subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, 
wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones as enumerated above the following recommendations 
as contained in its 131st Report wherein a time schedule for the laying of subordinate 
legislation has been prescribed as follows: 
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the publication of 
the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before 
the expiry of  the  Session immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply with this 
schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued under various Acts of Parliament 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
  
 4.        The Committee also reiterates its following observations made in its 135th Report 
regarding appending of delay statement where there has been delay in the laying: 

 “ The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there 
is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so as to 
apprise the Parliament of the causes of delay.  The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this,   since   the intention is that through the 
process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, identifying 
bottlenecks and devising remedial measures”.

INTRODUCTION 
       I, the Chairman of the Committe e on Subordinate Legislation, having been 
authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this 
Hundred and Forty Eighth Report of the Committee. 
1.2The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on 7th August, 
2003. 
1.3The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the Table of the Rajya 
Sabha during its 198th session have been perused by the Committee in the light of the 
provisions of the Acts under which these were framed and also with a view to seeing 
whether these have been laid properly and within the prescribed time -frame. The 
Committee's observations/recommendations are contained in the report that follows. 
New Delhi; 
7th August, 2003 
A.VIJAYARAGHAVAN 
Chairman 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya 
Sabha. 
  
 
REPORT 
I 
Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of Rajya Sabha 

      During the 198th Session of the Rajya Sabha, 592 Statutory Orders were laid on the 
Table of the House by various Ministries/Departments. The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were publ ished and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise statement placed at Annexure. 
2.   During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted some cases 
where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of notification of the Order 
and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in 
cases where notifications have not been laid as per the Committee's guidelines and 
whether such notification s were accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons for 
the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has been quite abnormal. The 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee in respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows :– 
I.    Ministry of Coal 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry of Coal have delayed the laying of 1 of their 
notifications (Sl. No. 14) out of the 4 notifications laid by them during the Session. The 
Ministry have also not appended any delay statement  with the notification. The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Coal shall adhere to the time schedule as 
recommended by the Committee in laying the Subordinate Legislation pertaining to 
them. 
II.   Ministry of Commerce & Industry 
      The Committee regr ets to note that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry have 
delayed the laying of 6 of their notifications (Sl. No. 18 & 31 to 35) out of the 22 
notifications laid by them during the 198th session. Notification at Sl. No. 18 was not even 
accompanied by a delay statement. Appropriately, notifications at Sl. Nos. 31 to 35 could 
have been laid during Monsoon (196th) Session or thereafter during Winter (197th) 
Session of 2002. The Ministry have practically laid these notifications after about one year 
of their publication. The delay statement of the Ministry is also not convincing as it simply 
states that sufficient time was not available during the Winter Session which had resulted 
in delay. The Committee is extremely unhappy to note that the Ministry of Commerce & 
Industry did not comply with the time schedule laid by the Committee for laying of 
Subordinate Legislation. The Committee recommends the Ministry of Commerce and 
Industry should stick to the time schedule as recommended by the Committee in its 131st 
Report in laying the Subordinate Legislation before the Parliament. 
III.Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution 
      The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & 
Public Distribution have delayed the laying of 2 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 49 & 50) 
out of the 7 notifications laid by them during the Session. The notification at Sl. No. 50 
could have been laid during theWinter (197th) Session and the notification  at Sl. No. 49 
even before i.e., during the Monsoon (196th) Session, 2002. Further, the delayed 
notifications were not accompanied by delay statements. The Committee would like to 
draw attention of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution towards 
the schedule prescribed by it in the matter of laying of Subordinate Legislation and it 
hopes that this would be complied with in future. 
IV.Ministry of Environment and Forests 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry of Environment and Forests have delayed the 
laying of 2 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 54 & 55) out of the 5 notifications laid by them 
during the session. There had been a delay of approximately 4 & 5 months in laying the 

notifications and no delay statements had been appended  to the notifications. The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Environment and Forests would observe the time 
schedule prescribed by it for laying of Subordinate Legislation in future. 
V.  Ministry of Finance 
      The Committee is extremely unhappy to note that the Ministry of Finance have again 
not complied with the schedule for laying of the notifications as prescribed by the 
Committee. The Ministry have laid 349 rules/regulations during the 198th session and 
there has been delay in case of 38 notificat ions ranging from 3 months to 10 months. 
Besides, there are 7 cases of delay exceeding one year (Sl. Nos. 104, 296 to 301) and one 
case of delay exceeding two years (Sl. No. 193). Further there has been one case of 
exceptional delay in laying (Sl. No. 264) where there has been a delay of 6 years. The delay 
statements have been appended only in 11 cases. In case of the notification at Sl. No. 264 
where there is a delay of over 6 years, the Ministry in their delay statement have simply 
stated that the reasons for delay were "not willful". This is not an acceptable explanation 
for delay. In another case (Sl. No. 273) the statement of delay as appended by the Ministry 
states – "Notification No. 16/2002 Service Tax dated 2.8.2002 could not be laid on the 
Table of  Rajya Sabha in the last session because of certain unforeseen circumstances 
beyond the control of the section."  The reason of delay given by the Ministry is not 
convincing. In other two cases (Sl. Nos. 322 & 323), the statement of delay appended by 
the Ministry states – "the notifications were sent on 12.12.2002 for laying before the Rajya 
Sabha for 17.12.2002 and Lok Sabha for 20.12.2002. The Rajya Sabha Secretariat refused 
to accept the same for laying due to shortage of time, and the house adjourned on 
21.12.2002. Hence the delay". In this context, it is stated that the last date of receiving 
notifications for laying on 17.12.2002 was 11.12.2002 and the notifications were brought 
to the Rajya Sabha Secretariat on 12.12.2002 i.e. after the due date. Further, the date of 
publication of both these notifications were 14.8.2002 and 30.9.2002 respectively, and 
evidently these could have been laid during the Winter (197th) Session or the first half of 
the Budget Session. Hence, the reasons of delay attributed by the Ministry of Finance are 
not justified. It may be recalled that the Committee had heard the Secretary, Ministry of 
Finance on the question of non -compliance of the time schedule in the matter of timely 
laying of Subordinate Legislation on the 9th Janua ry, 2003. During the course of oral 
evidence, the Finance Secretary, while admitting delay in laying, had assured the 
Committee that they shall take appropriate remedial action to avoid delay in future. The 
Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and would take concerted 
steps to eliminate such instances of delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation in future. 
VI.Ministry of Home Affairs 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry of Home Affairs have delayed the laying of 
one of their notification (Sl. No. 404) by 6 months and no delay statement was annexed. 
The notification could have been laid during the preceding (197th) session. The 
Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and ensure compliance 
with time schedule for laying the notifications in future. 
VII.   Ministry of Human Resource Development 
      The Committee notes with regret that there is delay in laying of 2 out of the 3 
notifications laid by the Ministry of Human Resource Development during the 198th  
Session (Sl. Nos. 407 & 408). The notifications having been published on the 18th 
November, 2002, the Ministry could have laid them during the 197th (Winter) Session, 
2002 itself. The Ministry also failed to append the requisite delay statement with both 
these notifications. There had been instances of delay in laying in some cases during the 

194th, 195th & 197th Sessions also. The Committee would like the Ministry to take 
necessary corrective measures so as to avoid such instances of delay in future. 
VIII.Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
      The Committee notes with regret that the only notification (Sl. No. 410) laid by the 
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has been delayed by 4 months and no delay 
statement has been enclosed therewith. The C ommittee hopes that the Ministry of 
Information & Broadcasting shall adhere to the time schedule as recommended by it for 
laying the Subordinate Legislation before the Parliament. 
IX.Ministry of Labour 
      The Committee notes with regret that there is a delay of over two years in laying of 1 
out of 4 notifications laid by Ministry of Labour (Sl. No. 411). The Committee takes note 
of the explanation for delay as given by the Ministry in the delay statement and hopes 
that such instances of delay shall not occur in future. 
X.  Ministry of Power 
      The Committee notes with regret that there is delay in laying of 1 out of the 2 
notifications laid by the Ministry of Power by 5 months and the Ministry have not 
appended any delay statement. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would ensure 
strict compliance of the schedule for laying Subordinate Legislation as prescribed by the 
Committee in its 131st report. 
XI.Ministry of Railways 
      The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Railways have laid 7 
rules/regulations during the 198th session out of which 5 have been delayed by period 
ranging from 5 months to one year. There were instances of delayed laying during the 
197th session also. Further, the Ministry have appended delay statement only in one case 
(Sl. No. 424). The Committee expects the Ministry to be cautious in such matters and 
ensure compliance with time schedule for laying the notifications in future. 
XII.   Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
      The Committee notes that the Ministry o f Road Transport and Highways have 
delayed in laying of 12 notifications out of the total of 143 notifications laid. The delay in 
laying range from 4-5 months and the Ministry have also appended reasons for delay in 
laying with these notifications during t he 198th session. The Committee expects the 
Ministry to be more prompt and vigilant in laying the rules/regulations within the 
stipulated period to obviate such instances of delay in future. 
XIII.Ministry of Shipping 
      The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Shipping delayed the laying of 
2 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 570 & 577) by 5 to 6 months. The Ministry also did not 
enclose the delay statements giving reasons for delay in laying. The Committee expects 
the Ministry of Shipping to exercise caution in such matters and ensure the laying of 
Subordinate Legislation within the time schedule. 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate 
steps to avoid delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation. The Co mmittee, accordingly, 
wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones as enumerated above the following recommendations, as 
contained in its 131st Report wherein a time schedule for the laying of Subordinate 
legislation has been prescribed, as follows : 

      "Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication of the 
Order in t he Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the 
publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the 
date of publication and the date of closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, 
before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth comply with this 
schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued under various Acts of Parliament 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha." 
4.   The Committee also reiterates its following observations made in its 135th Report 
regarding appending of delay statement where there has been delay in the laying : 
          "The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is  essential that in case 
there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so as 
to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committ ee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the 
process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, identifying 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures".
