Definitions  
“COURT” MEANS- 
  
(i)                  In any town or city, where there is a City Civil Court having 
ordinary Original Civil Jurisdiction, by that Court; 

  
(ii)                In town or city, where there is no such City Civil Court, by the High 
Court; 
  
(iii)               Elsewhere, also by any District Judge or by any Judge of the 
principal Court of Civil Jurisdiction”. 
  
The word `Court’ has not been defined properly in regulations 2 (1) (d). Sub-
clause (ii) appears unnecessary, as there would be a civil court having jurisdiction in all 
cases.  There appears to be some defect in the definition as the word ‘by’ appearing at 
different places is unnecessary.  Whether the Ministry would correct the same? 
  
            Ministry’s Comments 
            In view of the observations of Committee on Subordinate Legislation and 
Ministry of Law it has been proposed to modify the definition of the term “Court” as 
under: 
            “Court” means the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in a district 
(which includes the High Court in exercise of its original civil jurisdiction), having 
jurisdiction to decide the questions forming the subject matter of the claims if the same 
have been the subject matter of a suit, but does not include any civil court of a grade 
inferior to such principal civil court, or any court of small causes. 
            Note: This definition has been virtually adopted from a recent parliamentary 
enactment, namely, the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. 
  
4.         Point referred: 
Regulation 4(1)(a)  
Procedure to be followed on Application for certain reliefs: 
  
“(1) Where an application has been made seeking one or more reliefs mentioned 
in sub-regulation (1) of regulation 3, the Court shall, along with issue of notic e to 
the defaulter under regulation 5,- 
  
(a) in the case of an Application seeking relief under clause (a) thereof, pass an 
interim Order, attaching the security furnished to the National Dairy Development 

Board, and so much of any other property of the defaulter as would, on being sold, 
realise an amount equivalent in value to the outstanding liability of the person to the 
Board, together with the costs of the proceedings” 
  
(i)                               Under section 31(1)(a) of the NDDB Act, 1987 any officer of the 
Board may apply to the court for an order for the sale of the property pledged 
mortgaged hypothecated or assigned to NDDB as security for the loan or 
advance.  There is no mention of any interim order in the Act.  Therefore, how 
rule 4(1) (a) mentions about passing of an interim order.  Should this power not 
be provided in the Act itself? 
  
(ii)                             Rule 4(1)(a) has the effect of giving directions to the court to pass an 
interim order attaching the security and also order the costs of the 
proceedings.  There is no mention of such provisions in the Act.  Therefore how 
under a rule such a provision can be made; Whether the Ministry would 
explain? 
  
            Ministry’s Comments 
               In view of the observations of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya 
Sabha, it is proposed to modify the regulation in such a way so as to leave it to the 
discretion of the Court to pass appropriate orders to ensure the ultimate recovery of the 
security amount. 
5.         Point referred: 
           Regulations 4(4) 
Procedure to be followed on Application for certain reliefs: 
  
 “Every application made under sub regulation (1) shall, save as provided herein, 
be   treated on par    with an    Application  for    execution   of   a   
valid decree of Court in favour of the National Dairy Development Board and 
against the defaulter, and the provisions of the Code shall mutates mutandis 
apply.” 
  
            What is the justification of treating the application (for interim relief) made 
under these regulations at par with an application for execution of valid decree of 

court?  How such provisions have been made in the regulations in the absence of 
corresponding provisions in the Act.  Would it not be more appropriate to provide for 
such things in the Principal legislations; what are the comments of the Ministry? 
  
            Ministry’s Comments 
            In view of the observations of Committee, it is proposed to delete the same from 
the Regulations. 
  
6.         Point referred: 
Regulations 9 & 10 
             
In the above regulations there is mention of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 
7.  But there is no sub-regulation (1) in regulation 7.  Whether the Ministry would 
rectify the position. 
   
            Ministry’s Comments 
            The mistake pointed out by the Committee will be rectified. 
  
            The Committee considered the matter in its meeting held on the 7th May 
2003.  The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry have agreed to take necessary 
action based upon its suggestions in relation to (i) modification of definition of the word 
‘Court’ in Regulation 2(1)(d) which was not proper in the opinion of the Committee; (ii) 
procedure to be followed on application for certain relief’s by leaving it to the discretion 
of court to pass appropriate orders by modifying Regulation 4(1) (a) and by deleting 
Regulation 4(4); and (iii) rectification of mistakes referred to in Regulations 7(1), 9 & 
10. 
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry would carry out the above amendments 
expeditiously. 
 

VI 
SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS 
I 
The Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 
  
The Committee at its meeting held on the 20 th May, 2003 considered the matter 
and noted the above comments of the Ministry on point no. 8 and 11. The Committee 
notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have since carried out and notified the following 
amendments in the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 as per its suggestions vide notification 
G.S.R. 21 (E) dated the 11 th January, 2002, publishing the Mineral Concession 
(Amendment) Rules, 2002: 
  
(i) Schedule II 
[Rule 9(2)(a)] 
By reasonably revising the application fee for prospecting 
licenses- (i) to rupees two hundred and fifty for first 
square kilometer or part thereof; and (ii) rupees fifty for 
each additional square kilometer as suggested by the 
Committee; 
  
(ii) Rule 14(1)(i) By substituting the words 'being not less than fifty paise 
and not more than five rupees' with the words 'being not 
less than rupee one and not more than rupees ten' thereby 
suitably revising the prescribed fee payable by the 
licensee; 
  
(iii) Rule 20(1) By substituting the words 'a sum of five hundred rupees' 
with the words 'a sum of two thousand and five hundred 
rupees' thereby suitably revising the security deposit

(iv) Rule 22(1)&3(i) by substituting the words 'a non refundable fee of five

(v) Rule 37(2) & 45 By omitting clause (ii) of rule 45 where reference to rule

(vi) Rule 44(i) By substituting the words 'being not less than fifty paise

licensee. 
             
II  
The Cochin Port Trust Employees (CCA) Regulations, 1964 
  
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have agreed to the 
Committee’s suggestions and carried out the amendments as under: - 
(i)   In Regulation 3(3) by substituting the words “whose decision thereon shall be 
final”  by the word “for decision”. The Committee had objected to the vesting of 
power to take final decision with the Central Government; 
  
(ii) Deleting Regulation 4 being superfluous; 
  
(iii) In Regulation 9(3) deleting the words  “whether on a criminal charge or 
otherwise” being superfluous; 
  
(iv) In Regulation 10(ii) by providing a minimum period of 6 months and the 
maximum period of 3 years for withholding of increments or promotion and by

(v) In Regulation 10(iv) by restricting the reduction to a lower grade or post for a

(vi) In Regulation 12(2) by substituting the words “within such time as may be

(vii) In Regulation 12(14) by inserting the words “within a period of 30 days” after

orders of the disciplinary authority. 
  
III 
The Vishakhapatnam Port Employees (GPF) Regulations, 1993 
  
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry has notified the

      a)    Regulation 2(5)(ii) by substituting the words “Head of the Department” by the

      b)    Regulation 2(5) by amending the definition of the word “child” so as to include

      c)    Regulation 4(1) by specifying the position in the regulation itself with regard to

Rules framed under the Foreign Exchange Management  
Act, 1999

2.   During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted 
some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of notification 
of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period 
of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by 
the Committee and whether such notifications were accompanied by a statement 
indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay 
has been quite abnormal. Th e observations/recommendations of the Committee in 
respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows:---- 
(i)    Ministry of Agriculture 
        The Committee notes that the laying of notifications at Sl. Nos.3-12 of the Annexure 
by the Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying) has 
been delayed by 1 year 3 months to 1 year 5 months four of them having been notified on 
the 10th September, 2002 and the rest on the 25th October, 2002. The regulations could 
have easily been laid during the 197 th, 198th or the 199th session of the Rajya Sabha. The 
Ministry has failed even to append the delay statements to the notifications. The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Animal 
Husbandry and Dairying) would in future adhere to the time schedule as 
recommended by it in its 131 st Report in the matter of laying of the Subordinate 
Legislation pertaining to their Department. 
(ii)   Ministry of Civil Aviation 
      The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Civil Aviation have 
delayed the laying of 4 of their notifications (Sl. No. 14 -17) out of the 6 
notifications laid by them during the 200th session. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation should stick to the time schedule as recommended by it in its 
131st Report in laying the Subordinate Legislation before the Parliament. 
(iii) Ministry of Finance 
        The Committee is unhappy to note that out of 388 notifications laid  by the Ministry 
of Finance during the 200 th session, there has been a deviation from the given schedule, 
in case of 73 notifications listed at serial numbers 64-65, 73-84, 126-135, 237-283 and 349-
350 of the Annexure. It is a matter of regret that in quit e a few of these cases the 
delay ranges between 6 months and 2 years 9 months. In percentage terms, the 
Committee regrets to note that there has been an increase in the cases of delay in laying 
of rules/regulations. While the percentage of delayed cases wa s around 6% during the 
197th session and 7.43% during 198 th session, it had risen to 15.25% during the 199 th 
session and further to 19% during the 200th session. 
        The Committee further notes that most of the notifications that have been delayed 
pertain to the Banking Division and as can be seen from the statement of reasons for delay 

which have been appended with some of these notifications, the delay has taken place due 
to delayed receipt of the notifications from the Gramin / Regional Banks or from  the 
Government Press. The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Finance have 
again failed to strictly adhere to the time schedule prescribed in its 135 th Report. The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance would put effective mechanism in place. 
(iv) Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has 
considerably reduced the delay in the laying of the notifications and mostly the delay 
ranges between 6 -7 months only and  out of the 149 notifications laid by them 
during the 200th session, there is a delay in laying of 10 notifications ( Sl Nos. 500-501 and 
507-514). The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry have appended delay 
statements to all the notifications. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would continue 
with their efforts and would be able to achieve the target of timely laying of all their 
subordinate legislation. 
3.   The Committee notes that there has been a delay in laying of one notification 
each by the Ministries of Culture (Sl. No. 60). Health and Family Welfare (Sl. No. 455) , 
Home Affairs (Sl. No. 462) , Human Resource Development (Sl. No. 470), Labour 
and Employment (Sl. No. 478) , Law and Justice (Sl. No. 488) , Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensio ns (Sl. No. 489) , Shipping (Sl. No. 658) , Textiles (Sl. No. 662)  and 
Urban Development (Sl. No. 666) . The delay in these cases range from  
6 months to 5 years 10 months and in most of the cases the Ministries have not appended 
delay statement along with the notification. The Committee hopes that the above 
Ministries would adhere to the time schedule for laying of the notification and also 
append therewith a delay statement in case of any delay in laying thereof. 
4.   Besides the timely laying of subordinate legislation, the Committee have 
come across instances where some Ministries/Departments have notified their 
rules/regulations bearing identical notification number for different notifications. 
Besides, there are some notifications without any notification number. Some such 
instances are as follows:----

5.     In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity. Similarly, no notification should 
be published/laid, which does not carry a notification number. The Committee 
expects all Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this  
regard. In case where there are more than one notification under a single file, the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file number on each notification 
should be suitably distinguished from one another. The Committee also impresses 
upon the Ministry of Urban Development to take care of these aspects and ensure 
that all rules/regulations published by them in the Gazette of India do carry distinct 
notification/file numbers so that they are identifiable at later stage. 

6.     The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate 
steps to avoid delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation. The Committee, 
accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the 
Government of Ind ia, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 131th and 135th Reports: 
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following the d ate of publication of the 
Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the 
publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag 
between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Ses sion is less 
than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the orders issued under v arious 
Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
(131st Report) 
“The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there 
is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so 
as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the 
process of formulation  of a delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, 
identifying bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135th Report)

152nd Report on Statutory Orders laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha during the 200 th 
Session. During the course of interaction, it was observed that the number of cases of 
delay in the laying of notifications by some of the Ministries/Departments was quite 
substantial and that there was a considerable scope for improvement. In this context, the 
Committee, however, noted that the practice of reporting to the House on the laying of 
Subordinate Legislation on the Table of the House on a sessional basis was not very old 
and that ever since the introduction of this practice, there has been considerable 
improvement both with regard to the timely laying as well as the format of the 
notifications. The Committee further noted that it had, in the past already, heard the 
Secretaries of the Mi nistries of Finance, Industry and Home Affairs on the question of

Committee felt that there was still a substantial delay in laying of rules/regulations in a

defaulting Ministries/ Departments so that the matter could be taken up with them. With

INTRODUCTION 
         I, the Chairman of the Committee on Sub ordinate Legislation, having been 
authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this 
Hundred and Fifty-Third Report of the Committee. 
1.2    The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the 16 th 
September, 2004. 
1.3    The matters examined by the Committee arise out of the scrutiny of various 
Rules/Regualtions and issues, related therewith, along with the comments of the 
Governments received thereon. The observations and recommendations which, i n the 
opinion of the Committee, should be brought to the notice of the House, are contained in 
the succeeding paragraphs of the Report. 
  
NEW DELHI; 
September 16, 2004 
A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN 
Chairman, 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
 Rajya Sabha. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
------------- 
REPORT 
I 
THE COCONUT DEVELOPMENT BOARD REGULATIONS, 1982— 
IMPLEMENTATION OF THE 126TH REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE 
        The Committe e considered the Coconut Development Board Regulations, 1982 
framed under the Coconut Development Board Act, 1979 and made some 
observations/recommendations in its 115 th report presented to the House on 24 th 
November, 1997. The Committee considered impleme ntation of these recommendations 
and presented its 126 th Report to the House on the   23rd December, 1999 and made the 
following observations/ recommendations: 
        “The Committee notes that necessary action has been taken on all recommendations 
of the C ommittee except one relating to Coconut Board Service Regulations. The 
Committee expresses its dissatisfaction over the fact that the Ministry of Agriculture 
could not keep its promise of framing the Coconut Board Service Regulations within four 
months as assured to the Committee during its visit to Cochin in January, 1999. The 
Committee hopes that the Coconut Development Board Service Regulations would be 
framed by the Ministry of Agriculture at the earliest under intimation to it.” 
2.     Extracts from th e above report were forwarded to the Ministry of Agriculture on 
the 28th January, 2000. In response, the Ministry of Agriculture vide their communication 
dated the 6th July, 2001 informed as follows:---- 
        “This Ministry has been examining the implic ations of a directive of the Finance 
Ministry issued vide their letter dated the 16 th March, 2000 about the introduction of 
pension scheme and regulation of pension in respect of the employees of the autonomous 
bodies under various Ministries. The guidelin es of the Finance Ministry in this letter 
stipulated that introduction of pension scheme on Government of India pattern to the 
employees of autonomous bodies should not be agreed to as a Rule and any exception in 
this regard should be referred to the Finance Ministry. 

        In view of the above, the draft Service Regulations for the Coconut Development 
Board employees were referred to the Finance Ministry who in turn had asked for certain 
facts to be furnished to them for consideration of the case. The De partment has already 
resubmitted the proposal. Based on the outcome further action will be taken by this 
Ministry in this matter.” 
3.     The Committee again discussed the subject matter with the representatives  
of the Coconut Development Board and the Ministry of Agriculture on the 11th July, 2001 
at Thiruvanthapuram during the course of its study visit. The Committee was informed 
that the stand taken by the Ministry of Finance was in conflict with the provision 
contained in the Coconut Development Board (CDB) Rules (Rule 20) which provides that 
the employees shall be governed by the service conditions including pension as applicable 
to the Central Government Employees of comparable status till separate Regulations 
were framed. It was further stated that su ch a change in service conditions could have 
only prospective effect and should be applicable only to those who came in service after 
the implementation of the decision. The existing employees should have the protection 
available under the CDB Rules. It was, accordingly, submitted before the Committee that 
the legal implications of the stand of the Ministry of Finance vis-a-vis the relevant 
statutory provisions of the CDB Act and Rules need to be examined by the Ministry of 
Law and Justice because, as per t he existing service conditions, the employees of the 
Board were eligible for pension and other benefits and conditions of service similar to the 
Central Government employees. The Chairman, Coconut Development Board was of the 
view that those conditions could not be changed adversely and legal complications could 
arise if the conditions of service relating to pension were changed in a way detrimental to 
the interest of the employees and/or the pensioners of the Board which include employees 
who were transfer red from the erstwhile Directorate of Coconut Development to the 
Board. Relevant extracts from the study note on the above discussions were forwarded to 
the Ministry of Agriculture on the 1st November, 2001. 
4.     The Ministry of Agriculture informed the Committee on the 20 th November, 2001 
that the matter was being taken up with the Ministry of Finance. They had sought certain 
clarifications which were furnished to them and the matter was pending with them. The 
Ministry also sought extension of time up to the 31st December, 2001 which was granted. 
The Action Taken Note received from the Ministry is enclosed (Annexure-I). 
5.     The Ministry of Agriculture vide their communication dated the 25th January, 2002, 
communicated the following advice received from the Ministry of Finance: 
        “The proposal for the protection of the service conditions of the staff and officers is 
listed at Annexure-II (a list consisting of 42 officials only). Issues relating to creation of 
further posts and the service condition s of the staff who were to be appointed in future 
were not raised in the Cabinet Note. Accordingly, the Service Regulations, now proposed, 
may pro vide only for the protection of pensionery benefits in respect of 42 staff and 
officers as listed at Annexure-II. These officers and staff were in position on the date of 
the Cabinet Note i.e., the 15 th November, 1977. Posts created thereafter are not covered 
by specific cabinet approval for extended benefits and, therefore, employees appointed 
subsequently against these posts cannot be covered by pension.” 
6.     The Ministry of Agriculture, however, further informed that the matter was again 
being referred to the Ministry of Finance for protecting the interest of the existin g 
employees at least and in response thereto, the Ministry of Finance had advised them to 
obtain legal opinion from the Ministry of Law and Justice on the point as to whether the 
Coconut Development Board Act/Rules/Regulations were required to be amended i n 
order to implement the decision/advice of the Ministry of Finance. For that purpose, the 

Ministry sought further extension of time upto the 30 th April, 2002 which was duly 
granted. 
7.     The Ministry of Agriculture vide their communications dated the  
29th April, the 30 th July and 24 th October, 2002 informed the Committee about the 
progress of the further consultation with the Ministry of Law and Justice and the 
Ministry of Finance in the matter. Action Taken Notes received from them are enclosed 
as Annexures II, III  and IV. The Ministry vide their communication dated the 20 th 
January, 2003 informed the Committee as under : 
        “Ministry of Finance have turned down the proposal vide their Note dated the 11 th 
November, 2002. As this Department strongl y feels about the entitlement of pensionery 
benefits to the Coconut Development. Board employees in view of the existing provisions 
of the Coconut Development Board Act, the matter was once again taken up with the 
Finance Ministry.” 
8.     The Ministry vide their communication dated the 7 th May, 2003  
(Annexure-V) informed that the Finance Ministry had turned down the proposal  
reiterating their earlier stand of not extending equal entitlement of pensionary  
benefits to all the employees of the Coconut Develop ment Board. It was added that the 
Ministry of Agriculture were contemplating their further course of action. 
9.     The Ministry vide their communication dated the 17 th July, 2003 informed  
as under: 
        “The Ministry again has taken up this matter by m eans of D.O. letter from the 
Agriculture Ministry addressed to the Finance Minister dated the 4 th June, 2003. 
However, the Finance Minister in his reply dated the 25 th June, 2003 has informed that 
the Government has taken a conscious policy decision not to  extend pension schemes to 
employees of autonomous institutions of all Ministries and as such the Coconut Board 
when its service regulations are notified for all employees appointed subsequent to the 
creation of the Board as an autonomous body cannot be given pensionary benefits. 
        The matter has legal implications and is, therefore, being examined further in this 
Department.” 
10.   Keeping in view a dead lock like situation, the Committee heard the  
Secretaries of the Ministry of Agriculture (Departme nt of Agriculture and  
Cooperation); Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure) and Ministry of Law 
and Justice (Department of Legal Affairs) on the 3 rd September, 2003 with a view to 
resolving the issue. 
11.   The Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, apprised the Committee about the efforts so 
far made by that Ministry for framing the Coconut Development Board Service 
Regulations in consultation with the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Law and 
Justice. He stated that the staff regulations have t o be made in terms of Regulation - 17 
of the Coconut Development Board Regulation, 1982. The Finance Secretary deposed 
before the Committee that the service regulations were being finalized and considering 
the legal position and administrative difficulties  the employees recruited up to 
notification of the proposed service regulations would continue to get pension on the 
Government of India pattern and in terms of Government policy subject to the approval 
of the Finance Minister to whom the matter had since been put up. 
12.   The Coconut Development Board Employees (Conditions of Service)  
Regulations, 2003 were ultimately laid before the Rajya Sabha/Lok Sabha on the 12th and 
8th December, 2003 respectively by the Ministry of Agriculture amending Regulation 4(2) 
of the Coconut Development Board Regulations, 1982. These regulations provided inter 
alia that the pensionary benefits, if any, payable to the persons appointed after the date 

of commencement of these regulations shall be regulated as per the instructions issued by 
the Ministry of Finance from time to time in respect of autonomous bodies under the 
Central Government. 
        The Committee is unhappy to note that the notification of the Coconut Board Service 
Regulations has been delayed for so long despit e specific recommendations of the 
Committee, first in its 115th Report presented on the 24th November, 1997 and thereafter 
reiterated in its 126th Report presented to the House on the 23rd December, 1999. What is 
surprising is the fact that the Ministry of Finance had all along been objecting to allowing 
of the pension scheme on the Government of India pattern to the employees of the 
Coconut Development Board in utter disregard to the provisions of the Coconut 
Development Board Act as well as the regulation s framed thereunder. The Committee 
notes with regret that the Ministry of Agriculture approached the Ministry of Finance a 
number of times, but, every time the proposal was declined on the ground that they had 
taken a policy decision not to extend pension schemes to the employees of the autonomous 
institutions of all Ministries. The Committee is, however, satisfied that the Ministry of 
Finance reviewed their stand while tendering oral e vidence before it on the 3 rd of 
September, 2003 and agreed to concur wit h the proposal of the Ministry of Agriculture 
to allow the benefit of pension on the lines of the Government of India to the existing 
employees of the Coconut Development Board till the notification of the service 
regulations keeping in view the legal posi tion and the administrative difficulties of the 
employees which would have otherwise entailed. The Committee would have appreciated 
if the Ministry of Finance had given this consideration to the matter earlier when the 
Ministry of Agriculture had been appr oaching them repeatedly for clearing of the 
regulations along with the legal opinion which was in their favour. 

ANNEXURE-I 
ENCLOSED WITH M/O AGRICULTURE COMMUNICATION DATED THE 20TH 
NOVEMBER, 2001 
Horticulture Division 
Action Taken Report on the Notification of Coconut Development 
Board employees Service regulations as directed by the Rajya   
Sabha Committee on Sub-ordinate Legislation in their  
126th Report 
        This is about the notification of Service Regulations in respect of Coconut 
Development Board employees. The Rajya Sabha Committee on Subordinate Legislation 
while reviewing the Subordinate Legislation and amendments thereupon suggested 
formulation of Service Regulation for Board employees and notification of the same. The 
Coconut Devel opment Board follows the Rules of the Central Government for all 
purposes e.g., administrative, financial and other matters as provided in Regulation 17 
under Chapter IV of Coconut Development Board Regulations, 1982. 
2.     The Coconut Development Board f ormulated the draft Service Regulations and 
forwarded the draft proposal to the Central Government after obtaining the approval of 
the members of the Board. The proposal was examined by this Department in 
consultation with the various concerned departments of the Central Government namely, 
the Department of Personnel and Training first, and then Ministry of Labour among 
others. Suggestions/Views expressed by the Central Agencies were incorporated in the 
draft and revisions carried out. The Rajya Sabha Commi ttee held discussions with 
Chairman, Coconut Development Board during January, 1999 and reviewed the progress 
in the matter. Also extensive consultations with the Officials of the Coconut Development 
Board were held. The proposal was finally referred to th e Ministry of Law (Legislative 
Department) for vetting of the draft. The Law Ministry before vetting, invited the officials 
of this Department and Coconut Development Board for discussions. On receipt of the 
vetted draft from the Ministry of Law, this Depa rtment was in the process of finalising 
the notification of the draft service regulations. In the meanwhile Ministry of Finance, 
Department of Expenditure vide their letter dated 16th March, 2000 issued new guidelines 
about the introduction of pension sche me and regulation of pension in respect of the 
employees of autonomous bodies under various Ministries. The Finance Ministry in their 
letter dated 16th March, 2000 advised as below: 
        “We have been advising autonomous bodies under various Ministries/ Departments 
of the Government of India to continue to follow the Contributory Provident Fund 
Scheme through the Life Insurance Corporation of India base on voluntary contributions 
by the employees and without any contribution from the Government or the emp loyees 
may join the pension scheme introduced by the Ministry of Labour for the PF 
subscribers. It may please be noted that introduction of pension scheme on GoI pattern

Action Taken Report on the notification of Coconut Development Board employees 
Service Regulations as directed by the Rajya Sabha Committee on Subordinate

126th Report. 
        The Rajya Sabha Committee on Subordinate Legislation while reviewing the 
Subordinate Legislation and amendments thereupon suggested formulation of Service 
Regulation for Board employees and notification of the same. The Coconut Development 
Board follows the Rules of the Central Government for all purposes e.g., administrative, 
financial and other matters, as provided in Rule 20 of Coconut Development Board Rules, 
1981 and Regulation 17 under Chapter-IV of Coconut Development Board Regulations, 
1982. 
2.     As mentioned in the Action Taken Report forwarded earlier vide our letter dated 
20-11-2001, as well as our Office Memorandum dated 25th January, 2002 the matter was 
being pursued with the Ministry of Finance. The Finance Ministry advised that the 
Service Regulations for the Coconut Development Board employees now proposed for 
notification may provide only for the protection of pensionary benefits in respect of 42 
staff and officers as listed and in position on the date of the Cabinet Note i.e., 15-11-1977. 
Posts created thereafter are not covered by specific Cabinet approval, and, therefore, 
employees appointed subsequently against these posts cannot be covered by pension as 
applicable to Central Government employees. 
3.     This Department considers that existing employees should have protection as 
available under the Coconut Development Board Rule 20 of Coconut Development Board 
Rules, 1981 and Regulation 17 of the Coconut Development Board Regulations, 1982. The 
decision of Ministry of Finance should be effective only from prospective date for the 
officers and staff joining service after the notification of the proposed revised regulations. 
Any revision in service regulations, if t hese are detrimental to the interest of existing 
employees, will lead to numerous court cases. On this Finance Ministry informed that 
their earlier advice essentially meant that rules and regulations should be exactly in line 
with Cabinet approval and ther e is a need to adhere to what has been approved by the 
Cabinet. Accordingly, the Finance Ministry advised this Department to obtain legal 
opinion from Law Ministry as to whether Coconut Development Board Act, Rules and 
Regulations are required to be amende d in order to implement decision/advice of the 
Finance Ministry. The Law Ministry expressed that there does not appear any need to 
amend the Coconut Development Board Act, Rules and Regulations in implementing the 
decision/advice of the Ministry of Finance.  
4.     At present service conditions, etc., of Board’s employees are regulated under Rule 
20 of the Coconut Development Board Rules, 1981 and Regulation 17 of the Coconut 
Development Board Regulations, 1982. The Rule 20 states that conditions of service and 
other facilities and concessions in respect of. all employees appointed by the Board shall 
be regulated in accordance with such rules and regulations, as are for the time being 
applicable to officers and employees of Central Government till separate regulations are 
made by the Board. Similarly, Regulation 17 of the Coconut Development Board 
Regulations, 1982 provides for pay, leave, allowance, pension and retirement benefits, etc. 
and other service conditions in respect  of all employees of the Board to be regulated in 
accordance with rules and regulations as are for the time being applicable to officers and 
employees of the Central Government. This Department felt that as such all the officers 

and staff of Board, includi ng the 42 transferred from Directorate of Coconut 
Development recruited and appointed by the Board under powers drawn from Section 
7(6) of the CDB Act, 1979 are governed by the provisions of the Act, Rules and 
Regulations mentioned above. The Board is, therefore, obliged (Section 20(7) of the Act) 
to protect the service conditions of all the existing staff and officers, at par with Central 
Government employees since their service conditions are governed by the provisions of 
the existing rules and regulations of the Board. Ministry of Agriculture, therefore, again 
referred the case to the Ministry of Finance, The Ministry of Finance re -examined the 
proposal of this Department and decided not to agree to the proposal of Ministry of 
Agriculture to provide pensionary benefits to all existing employees of the Board.  
5.     This Ministry feels that if this decision of Ministry of Finance is implemented, there 
will be numerous court cases as it does not protect the benefits being enjoyed by all the 
existing employees of the Board as provided under Rule 20 of the Coconut Development 
Board Rules, 1981 and Regulation 17 of the Coconut Development Board Regulations, 
1982. The Ministry is, therefore, seeking advice of Ministry of Law whether curtailment 
of pensionary benefits being presently enjoyed by all the existing employees of the Board 
will not amount to contravention of the existing rules and regulations of the Coconut 
Development Board.

THE STATUTORY ORDER NO. 1076 (E) DATED THE 
DECEMBER 15, 1998 ISSUED UNDER THE JUTE PACKAGING 
MATERIALS (COMPULSORY USE IN PACKAGING COMMODITIES) 
ACT, 1987 — IMPLEMENTATION OF 127TH REPORTS 
OF THE COMMITTEE 
        The Committee examined the Statutory Order No. 1076 (E) dated the 15th December, 
1998 issued under the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing 
Commodities) Act, 1987 and included the subject matter in its 127 th Report which was 
presented to the Hou se on the 14 th March, 2000. The Committee in the said report 
observed as under: 
              “4.  The Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on 
February 23, 2000. The Committee notes with satisfaction that Government have 
been keeping in mind the interest of the jute farmers, workers and the end users by 
following the provisions of the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing 
Commodities) Act, 1987. The Committee, however, desires that the problems of the 
jute growers need to be looked into by Government more seriously so that they could 
get a fair return. In the opinion of the Committee, Government need to put in more 
efforts towards diversification and value addition in the Jute Sector so that the jute 
growers as well as the persons engaged in the trade in this sector are encouraged. 
              5.  As regards the constitution of the Standing Advisory Committee, the 
Committee is not in agreement with the position as stated by the Ministry of Textiles. 
The Committee feels that its suggestion to broad base the composition of the Standing 
Advisory Committee has the endorsement of the Apex Court of the country also and, 
therefore, there is all the more a ground to review the composition of the Standing 
Advisory Committee and amend the provisions of the Statutory Order. The Standing 
Advisory Committees might be inviting and hearing views of the concerned 
industries and user sectors while reviewing the mandatory Packaging Order, but in 
the opinion of the Committee representation of concerned industries and user sectors 
in the Standing Advisory Committee would lend better support to the cause.” 
2.     Relevant extracts from the 127 th Report were forwarded to the Ministry of Textiles 
for their comments/clarifications on the 21 st March, 2000. The Ministry on the 11 th 
August, 2000 informed as under: 
        “In accordance to the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court the Standing 
Committee is inviting comments and hearing the views of the concerned industries 
and user sectors after giv ing due notice through recognized office bearers of the 
associations, particularly when the question of review of the mandatory Packaging 
Order is considered. Their views are fully taken into account before taking any 
decision in this regard. The matter may therefore be treated as closed.” 
3.     The Committee at its meeting held on the 16 th May, 2002 considered the subject 
matter and expressed its dissatisfaction over the Ministry’s Action Taken Report in 
pursuance of its recommendation as contained in the  127th Report on the subject. The 
Committee noted that the Ministry had simply reiterated their earlier position and had 
not complied with the Committee’s recommendations to broad base the composition of 
the Standing Advisory Committee. The Committee decided that its recommendations on 
the subject be further reiterated. Accordingly, the Ministry was requested vide this 
Secretariat communication dated the 31st May, 2002 to review the position in the light of 
the Committee’s recommendations/observations and i ntimate the proposed course of 
action. 

4.     In response, the Ministry on the 21st October, 2002 requested for a copy of the Report 
as well as a copy of this Secretariat’s communication dated the 31st May, 2002 which were 
not traceable with them. These documents were duly furnished to the Ministry. 
5.     Thereafter, there was no response from the Ministry despite repeated reminders 
from this Secretariat until a D.O. letter was issued to the Secretary, Ministry of Textiles 
on the 7th July, 2003 requesting for the latest position with regard to the implementation 
of Committee’s pending recommendations. 
6.     The Ministry furnished the Action Taken Note on the 29 th July, 2003 stating as 
under: 
I.     Regarding interest of jute farmers, workers and users enga ged in the trade in the 
Jute Sector 
        “The Minimum Support Price (MSP) are fixed by the Government every year. The 
Minimum Support Price for TD-5 grade of jute growers in Assam had been raised from 
Rs. 810/- per quintal in 2001 -02 to Rs. 850/ - per quintal for the jute year 2002 -03. This 
has further been raised to Rs. 860/- per quintal for the jute year 2003-04. On the basis of 
MSP declared by Government, grade -wise price differentials are fixed by the Jute 
Commissioner for every jute year are being wi dely publicized through radio, television, 
newspapers and other media. 
        The Government of India has taken necessary steps towards diversification and 
value addition in the jute sector. In order to modernize the jute sector, Special Jute 
Development Programme (SJDF) with cent per cent Central Assistance has been 
launched. In addition, financial assistance is also provided under the Technology 
Upgradation Fund Schemes (TUFS). The Government also proposes to launch Jute 
Technology Mission (JTM) for the development of jute industry. For providing incentives 
to exporters, the Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB) Scheme has also been extended to 
the jute sector.” 
II.    Regarding constitution of the Standing Advisory Committee 
        “The recommendation has been noted and will be considered while constituting the 
new Standing Advisory Committee.” 
7.     The reply of the Ministry was found not satisfactory and they were asked vide this 
Secretariat communication dated the 24 th September, 2003 to review the matte r with a 
view to suitably modifying the provisions of rule 3 of the Jute Packaging Materials 
(Compulsory use in Packaging Commodities) Rules, 1987 as well as the relevant 
provisions of the Statutory Order so as to prescribe therein the concerned industries and 
user Sectors to be represented in the Standing Advisory Committee. 
8.     The Ministry vide their communication dated the 18 th December, 2003  
have since informed as under:---- 
        “The Ministry of Textiles has no objection in modifying the provisions of Rule 3 of 
the Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987 so that the concerned industries and user 
Sectors are to be represented in the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) after the 
expiry of the tenure of the SAC which was constituted in May, 2001 and will remain 
valid for a period of three years till May, 2004.” 
9.     Committee’s observations/recommendations 
        The Committee expresses its displeasure over the non -serious attitude of the 
Ministry of Textiles in implementing the recommendations of the Committee as contained 
in its 127 th Report as a result of which the Committee had to repeatedly approach the 
Ministry for eliciting a proper response. The Committee is rather shocked that the 
Ministry, in their initial action taken note on the Committ ee’s report, had simply 

reiterated their earlier stand and when they were asked to review the position, they did 
not have even a copy of the Committee’s report. 
        The Committee expects that the Ministry of Textiles would act more responsibly 
while dealing with the recommendations of the Committee. The Committee, however, 
notes that the Ministry of Textiles have ultimately agreed to amend the provisions of Rule 
3 of the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packaging Commodities) Rules, 
1987 in order to provide therein the industries and user sectors to be represented in the 
Standing Advisory Committee in pursuance of its recommendations.

under Regulation-2 should be incorporated in the Regulations. 
        Action Taken :  The Ministry have inserted regulatory Regulations providing as 
under 
        “The designated person shall grant or renew the licence within a period of three 
months from the date of application.” 
        Recommendation (ii) : That the reasons for the delay in grant/renewal of licence and 
the likely time for completing the process in regulation 3 (2) should be intimated to the 
applicant. 
        Action Taken  : The Ministry have inserted regulatory Regulations providing as 
under: 
        “The designated person shall, if the consideration of the application is likely to get 
delayed within 60 days of the receipt of application, inform the applicant the reasons 
for such a delay, and the likely time it would take to do so”. 
        Recommendation (iii) : That whenever an application is rejected, the reasons should 
be informed to the applicant. 
        Action Taken  : T he Ministry in their action taken note stated that the IRDA 
(Licensing of Insurance Agents) Regulations, 2000 already cover this recommendation 
under rule 3(3) which provides as under: 
“If the designated person refuses to grant or renew a license under this Regulation, 
he shall give the reasons therefor to the applicant”. 
        The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance, Insurance 
Division, have notified amendments in the Insurance Regulatory and Development 
Authority (Licensing of Insurance Agents) Regulations, 2000 as recommended by it.

------------- 

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS 
I 
THE COCONUT DEVELOPMENT BOARD REGULATIONS, 1982—
IMPLEMENTATION OF THE 126TH REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE ON 
SUBORDINATE LEGISLATION, RAJYA SABHA 
        The Committee is unhappy to note that the notification of the Coconut Board Service 
Regulations has been delayed for so long despit e specific recommendations of the 
Committee, first in its 115th Report presented on the 24th November, 1997 and thereafter 
reiterated in its 126th Report presented to the House on the 23rd December, 1999. What is 
surprising is the fact that the Ministry of Finance had all along been objecting to allowing 
of the pension scheme on the Government of India pattern to the employees of the 
Coconut Development Board in utter disregard to the provisions of the Coconut 
Development Board Act as well as the regulation s framed thereunder. The Committee 
notes with regret that the Ministry of Agriculture approached the Ministry of Finance a 
number of times, but, every time the proposal was declined on the ground that they had 
taken a policy decision not to extend pension schemes to the employees of the autonomous 
institutions of all Ministries. The Committee is, however, satisfied that the Ministry of 
Finance reviewed their stand while tendering oral evidence before it on the 3 rd of 
September, 2003 and agreed to concur wit h the proposal of the Ministry of Agriculture 
to allow the benefit of pension on the lines of the Government of India to the existing 
employees of the Coconut Development Board till the notification of the service 
regulations keeping in view the legal posi tion and the administrative difficulties of the 
employees which would have otherwise entailed. The Committee would have appreciated 
if the Ministry of Finance had given this consideration to the matter earlier when the 
Ministry of Agriculture had been appr oaching them repeatedly for clearing of the 
regulations alongwith the legal opinion which was in their favour. 
II 
THE STATUTORY ORDER NO. 1076 (E) DATED DECEMBER 15, 1998 
ISSUED UNDER THE JUTE PACKAGING MATERIALS (COMPULSORY 
USE IN PACKAGING COMMODITIES) ACT, 1987—IMPLEMENTATION 
OF 127TH REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE 
        The Committee expresses its displeasure over the non -serious attitude of the 
Ministry of Textiles in implementing the recommendations of the Committee as contained 
in its 127 th Report as a re sult of which the Committee had to repeatedly approach the 
Ministry for eliciting a proper response. The Committee is rather shocked that the 
Ministry, in their initial action taken note on the Committee’s report, had simply 
reiterated their earlier stand and when they were asked to review the position, they did 
not have even a copy of the Committee’s report. 
        The Committee expects that the Ministry of Textiles would act more responsibly 
while dealing with the recommendations of the Committee. The Co mmittee, however, 
notes that the Ministry of Textiles have ultimately agreed to amend the provisions of Rule 
3 of the Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packaging Commodities) Rules, 
1987 in order to provide therein the industries and user sectors  to be represented in the 
Standing Advisory Committee in pursuance of its recommendations. 
III 
THE OZONE DEPLETING SUBSTANCES (REGULATIONS & CONTROL) 
RULES, 2000—IMPLEMENTIATON OF 138TH REPORT OF COMMITTEE 

ON SUBORDINATE LEGISLATION, RAJYA SABHA 
        The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Environment & Forests 
have amended Rule 2 (h) (i) which contained a typographic error and added sub rules (8) 
and (9) to Rule 13 specifying a time limit of 60 days for registration, renewal and 
cancellation of registration as recommended by the Committee. 
IV 
THE MERCHANT SHIPPING (MANAGEMENT OF SAFE OPERATION 
OF SHIPS) RULES, 2000— IMPLEMENTATION OF 143RD REPORT OF THE 
COMMITTEE 
        The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have carried out and 
notified all the amendments as per its suggestions. 
V 
THE INSURANCE REGULATORY AND DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
(LICENSING OF INSURANCE AGENTS) REGULATIONS, 2000— 
IMPLEMENTATION OF 149TH REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON SUBORDINATE 
LEGISLATION, RAJYA SABHA 
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance, Insurance 
Division, have notified amendments in the Insurance Regulatory and Development 
Authority (Licensing of Insurance Agents) Regulations, 2000 as recommended by it.

be published/la id which does not carry a notification number. The Committee 
expects all Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this 
regard. In case where there are more than one notifications under a single file, the 
Ministries/Departments s hould ensure that the file number on each notification 
should be suitably distinguished from one another".

2.     During the course of scrutiny of these Notifications/Orders, the Committee has noted 
some cases of abnormal delay ranging from 2 to 6 years between the date of notification 
of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period 
of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by 
the Committee and also whether such notifications were accompanied by any statement 
indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. The observations/recommendations of the 
Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows:---- 
(i)     Ministry of Environment & Forests 
        The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Environment and Forests have 
delayed the laying of 6 of their notifications (Sl. No. 35 -37 and 41 -43) out of the 17 
notification laid by them during the 202 nd Session. The delay ranges between 10 months 
and 1 year 4 months. Further, the Ministry have appended the delay statement with 3 
notifications (Sl. No. 41 -43) only and the re maining 3 notifications (Sl. No. 35 -37) were 
not accompanied by delay statements. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
Environment & Forests should strictly adhere to the time schedule as recommended by 
it in its 131 st Report in laying of the Subo rdinate Legislation before Parliament and in 
case of any delay in laying of the notifications, a delay statement should also invariably 
be appended therewith. 
(ii)    Ministry of Finance 
        The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 320 notifica tions laid by the 
Ministry of Finance during the 202 nd Session, there has been a delay in laying of 27 
notifications listed at Sl. Nos. 51-55, 131-138, 139, 140-143, 144, 145-146, 147, 148-151 and 
152 of the Annexure. The period of delay range from a minim um of 9 months to the 
maximum of 3 years and 6 months. The Committee views with serious concern that in 
spite of its repeated recommendations regarding the timely laying of subordinate 
legislation, there has not been any appreciable improvement in the position. 

        The Committee further notes that all the delayed notifications pertain to the 
Department of Economic Affairs (Banking Division). The reasons for delay which have 
been appended with some of these notifications, such as, “copies of the notifications were 
not received in time” are also not plausible enough to justify the delay that range between 
1-3 years. The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Finance have again failed 
to strictly adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in its 13 1st Report. The Committee 
hopes that the Ministry of Finance would put an effective mechanism in place to eliminate 
such instances of delay in future, particularly on account of delay in receiving printed 
copies of the notifications. The Committee hopes th at the Ministry of Finance would be 
able to plug the loopholes so that delays do not recur in future. 
(iii)   Ministry of Information and Broadcasting 
        The Committee notes that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting laid two 
notifications (Sl.  Nos. 392 and 393) and both were delayed by more than one year. 
Further, the Ministry did not append any delay statement with these notifications. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting should take 
note of the time schedule as prescribed by it for laying of the Subordinate legislation and 
take necessary corrective steps so that such instances do not recur. 
(iv)   Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions 
        The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances 
and Pensions delayed the laying of 11 notifications (Sl. Nos. 409 -419) out of 16 laid by 
them during the 202nd Session. Further, none of the delayed notification was accompanied 
by a delay statement. The period of delay wa s also substantial, ranging between 1 to 2 
years. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances 
and Pensions should take necessary corrective steps in the right earnest so that they are 
able to lay their Subordinate Legislation  on time. The Committee further recommends 
that the Ministry should invariably apprise the House about the reasons for delay 
through delay statement in case they are unable to lay any ‘Order’ on time. 
3.     The Committee also notes that there has been delay in laying of one notification each 
by the Ministries of Health and Family Welfare (Sl. No. 371), Home Affairs (Sl. No. 376), 
Human Resource Development (Sl. No. 386), Labour and Employment (Sl. No. 394), 
Railways (Sl. No. 444), Shipping, Road Transport and Highways (Sl. No. 538) and Urban 
Development (Sl. No. 593). In case of notification at Sl. No. 538 (Ministry of Shipping, 
Road Transport and Highways) the delay is of 6 years and 11 months. Further, the 
notifications at Sl. Nos. 386, 394 and 593 were not accompanied by delay statements. The 
Committee hopes that these Ministries would devise appropriate measures to cut on the 
delay in    laying of the notifications. They should also be particular to append delay 
statement in case the laying of Subordinate Legislation is delayed. 
4.     Besides, the timely laying of Subordinate Legislation, the Committee has been 
consistently reiterating that each notification should have a distinctive number so that 
the same is identifiable. However, during the 202nd Sessi on the Committee has came 
across three instances where the notifications were laid without a distinct number. These 
notifications pertain to the Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Sl. 
No. 19), the Ministry of Finance (Sl. No. 132) and the  Ministry Human Resource 
Development (Sl. No. 390). The Committee reiterates that every notification should have 
a distinctive number to give it a separate identity. The Committee  recommends that such 
instances should not be repeated and Ministries/ Depar tments should ensure that every 
notification is assigned a distinct number so that the same is identifiable at any later stage. 
5. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps 
to ensure timely and proper laying of sub ordinate legislation. The Committee, 

accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the 
Government of India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following recommendations, 
as contained in its 131st, 135th and 152nd Reports: 
“Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid  
(i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the date 
of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, 
on the date of the p ublication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the 
time lag between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the 
said Session. All the  Ministries/Departments of Government of India should 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued 
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.”    
                                                                                    (131st Report) 
“The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there 
is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so 
as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the 
process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, 
identifying bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”.                                                                                   (135th Report) 
“In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects 
all Ministries/ Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this regard. 
In case where there are more than one notification under a single file, the Ministries/ 
Departments should ensure that the file number on each notification should be 
suitably distinguished from one another. 
                                                                                  (152nd Report)

 I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, 
having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its 
behalf, do hereby present this Hundred and Fifty Sixth Report of the 
Committee. 
1.2 The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its

1.3 The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. laid on the 
Table of the Rajya Sabha during its 203rd session (December, 2004) 

have been persued by the Committee in the light of the provisions of 
the Acts under which these were framed and also with a view to seeing 
whether these have been laid properly and within the prescribed time-
frame. The Committee's observations/recommendations are contained 
in the report that follows.

I

which these were published and the date of their laying on the Table of 
the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Mi nistry-wise statement 
placed at Annexure. Out of the above notifications, there has been delay 
in laying of 79 notifications as per the following statement:

2. During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has 
noted some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between 
the date of notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The 
annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in cases where 
notifications have not been laid as per the Comm ittee’s guidelines and 
whether such notifications were accompanied by a statement indicating 
the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has 
been quite abnormal. The observations/recommendations of the 
Committee in respect of the sp ecific Ministries/Departments are as 
follows: 
(i) Ministry of Agriculture 
 (Department of Agriculture and Cooperation) 
 The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 4 notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Agriculture and 
Cooperation) there has been a delay of upto 1 year in the laying of three 
notifications (Sl. Nos. 2, 3, 4 of the Annexure). The Ministry have not 
appended delay statement with any of these delayed notifications.  The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Agriculture (Department 
of Agriculture and Cooperation) should stick to the time schedule as 
recommended by it in its 131 st Report in the matter of laying of 
Subordinate Legislation before Parliament and in case of any delay, the 
delay statement must also be appended therewith. 
(ii) Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of 
Industrial 
 Policy and Promotion) 
 The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Commerce and 
Industry (Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion) have 
delayed the laying of 7 of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 
17,18,20,21,22,23,and 24) out of the 14 notifications laid by them during 
the session. The Ministry have not appended delay statement with six 
of the delayed notifications where the delay ranges from 6 months to 1 
year and three months. The Ministry have appended delay statement 
only with 1 notification (Sl. No.21) stating therein as follows: 
“The copy of the above notification could not be laid in the earlier 
session as the printed copies of the notification were not received 
in time. Subsequent session i.e. Budget Session of Parliament, 2004 
took place for one week only for vote on accounts. Next Parliament 

Session was convened during July-August, 2004 after constitution 
of the new Lok Sabha. At that time we missed th e laying down of 
the notification due to oversight. The delay is regretted”. 
 The Committee is not convinced with the grounds for delay 
furnished by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry in the delay 
statement. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would take 
necessary corrective measures to avoid delay in laying on such grounds 
and adhere to the schedule prescribed by the Committee in its 131st 
Report. 
(iii) Ministry of Communications and Information 
Technology 
 The Committee is unhappy to note that  out of the 20 notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, 
there has been a delay in the laying of 15. The Department of 
Telecommunications have delayed the laying of 2 notifications (Sl. Nos. 
26, 27) out of the 4 notifications laid by them and have appended delay 
statement with both. The delay statement appended to notification 
No.414/7/99-FA dated 23rd February, 2004 (Sl. No.26) states: “....After 
notification of the Regulation in the Official Gazette, TRAI sent the 
Regulation to the Department of Telecommunications on 4th October, 
2004. Accordingly, the reason for delay in laying the Regulation on the 
Table of the House is due to delayed submission to the Government”. 
The delay in laying of notification No. 414 - 7/99 - FA dated 25th May, 
2004 (SI. No. 27) has been attributed by the Ministry to the delay in 
making available the copies of the notifications to the Government. The 
Committee hopes that the Government would take necessary corrective 
measures to avoid such in stances of delay which are, even otherwise, 
not very convincing. 
 On the other hand, the Department of Information Technology 
have delayed the laying of 13 notifications (Sl. Nos. 29 to 41) out of the 
16 notification laid by them. The Committee regrets to note that the 
delay in the laying of the notifications by the Department of 
Information and Technology range from 9 months to around a year in 
some cases and upto 1 year and 9 months in others. The Ministry have 
even failed to append the delay statement to the notifications despite so 
much delay. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
Communications & Information Technology should avoid such delays 
in future and append delay statement where ever the schedule as laid 

down by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha in its 
131’t Report is not adhered to. 
(iv) Ministry of Company Affairs 
 The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 11 months 
in laying of one out of the five notifications laid by the Ministry of 
Company Affairs (Sl No. 47). The Committee hopes that the Ministry 
of Company Affairs would avoid such instances in future. 
(v) Ministry of Environment and Forests 
 The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Environment 
and Forests have laid 8 notifications during the ‘session and out of them 
4 (SI. Nos. 57, 60, 61, 62) have been delayed by a period of 4 to 7 months. 
Further, the Ministry have appended delay statement with only 2 of the 
delayed notifications (Sl. Nos. 61,62). The Committee observes that the 
delay in  laying of the Rules was “owing to the pre -mature sine die  
adjournment of the House.” The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Environment and Forests would take action at the first available 
opportunity so as to obviate such eventualities. 
(vi) Ministry of Finance 
 The Committee notes that out of the 211 notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Finance during the Winter Session, 2004, there has been a 
delay in the laying of 11 notifications (Sl Nos. 65, 66, 98 to 102, 124, 170 
to 172). The Committee further notes that the Ministry have appended 
delay statement in only two cases. While the delay in the laying of 
notification No. LEG -59/46 dated the 22nd July, 2004 (Sl. No.66) has 
been attributed to sine die  adjournment of the House, the delay 
statement appended to notification No 8/5/2004 - IF - I dated the 18th 
June, 2004 (Sl. No. 124) states as follows: 
 “Two notifications were sent to the Controller of Publications, 
Civil Lines, New Delhi vide letter dated 26th May, 2004 for 
publishing in the Gazette of India. One notification under sub -
section (1) of Section 18 of the Industrial Development Bank of 
India Act, 1964 and another notification under sub -section (2) of 
Section 21 of the said Act. 
 Ministry of Urban Development, Dep artment of Publications 
Civil Lines has forwarded one notification vide letter dated 12th 
July, 2004. It was found that only one notification under Section 18 

of the IDBI Act, 1964 had been published and the other notification 
under Section 21 of the said Act had not yet been published. A 
reminder was sent to the Controller of Publication, Civil Lines vide 
letter dated 26th July, 2004. Therefore, these notifications could not 
be laid on the Table  of both Houses of Parliament during 
Budget Session of Parliament. 
 After authentication by Minister of State (R), the notification 
will be laid on the Table of both Houses of Parliament during the 
Winter Session of Parliament.” 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance would avoid 
such instances of delay in  the laying of Subordinate Legislation and 
shall keep the House informed of the reasons for delay in laying 
through delay statements in all cases. 
(vii) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Health and 
Family Welfare have delayed the laying of one notification (Sl. No. 276) 
by 9 months out of the 2 notifications laid during the Session. The 
Ministry have appended a delay statement. The Committee would like 
to draw the attention of the Ministry of Health an d Family Welfare to 
the Schedule prescribed by the Committee in the matter of laying of 
Subordinate Legislation in its 131st Report (relevant extracts 
reproduced in para 3 of the report) and hopes that the same shall be 
complied with. 
(viii) Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions 
 The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel, 
Public Grievances & Pensions have laid 26 notifications during the 
Session out of which 12 (Sl. Nos. 289 to 300) have been delayed by 
almost 1 year. The Ministry have appended delay statement with all the 
12 delayed notifications. In their delay statement appended to the 
notification at Sl. No. 300 of the Annexure the Ministry have submitted 
as follows: 
 “The Notification which was sent to the Government o f India 
Press for Publication in Part II section 3(i) of the Gazette of India 
on 5th November, 2003 was published in the Gazette on 13th 
December, 2003, i.e. during the Winter Session of Parliament, 
2003. Therefore it was not possible to lay the notificati on during 
the Winter Session of Parliament, 2003. 

 The notification was sent for laying on the Table of the Lok 
Sabha/Rajya Sabha during the Budget Session of Parliament 2004, 
which commenced from the 5th July, 2004 and scheduled to end on 
September, 2004. However, due to pre -mature sine-die 
adjournment of Parliament on 26 th August, 2004, the notification 
could not be laid on the Table of the House”. 
 The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Personnel, 
Public Grievances & Pensions could not avail of the opportunity to lay 
the Subordinate Legislation not only during the Winter Session 2003 
but also during the Budget Session 2004 which actually had 22 sittings. 
In any case, had the Ministry acted promptly they could have 
accomplished their job in the earlier part of the Budget Session 2004. 
The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensions would be meticulous in future in complying 
with time schedule as prescribed by the Committee and take prompt 
action, rather than keeping the work pending towards the end of the 
Session. 
(ix) Ministry of Railways 
 The Committee notes with regret that out of the 13 notifications 
laid by the Ministry of Railways, there has been a delay in the laying of 
11 notifications (Sl. Nos.324 to 334). The Committee expects the 
Ministry of Railways to exercise caution in the matter of timely laying 
of subordinate Legislation and ensure that the schedule as prescribed 
by it in this behalf is followed  meticulously and in case of any delay in 
the laying thereof, a delay statement must be appended there with 
without fail. 
(x) Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways 
 The Committee regrets to note that out of a total of 92 notifications 
laid by M inistry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways, during 
the 203rd Session there has been a delay in the laying of 13 notifications 
(SI. Nos.336, 343 to 352, 424 and 426). The delay in laying of the 
notifications ranges between 5 months to 1 year. The Comm ittee 
observes that while notification No. D1201 1/1/98 - TAMP at Sl. No. 426 
of the annexure could not be laid during the Budget Session due to sine 
die adjournment of Parliament, the delay statement appended to the 
rest of the delayed notifications does not carry convincing reasons. The 
delay statement appended to one set of notifications (S.O. 751 (E), 

S.0.862 (E) to S.0.868 (E), S.0.885 (E); S.O. 579 (E), S.0.811 (E), S.0.912 
(E), S.0.934 (E), S.0.935 (E) and S.0.938 (E)) states, “It took some time 
to collect the papers and complete the procedural formalities”. For 
example the delay statement appended to G. 5.R.83 (E) dated the 28 th 
January, 2004 states, “Since the requisite number of copies of the 
printed notifications were not received in time, the sa me could not be 
laid on the Table of the House.” The Committee directs the Ministry of 
Shipping, Road Transport and Highways to be more prompt and 
vigilant in the laying of rules/regulations within the stipulated period 
and evolve some systematic procedure to avoid such instances in future. 
3. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to 
take immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate 
legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice 
of all Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, 
the defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 
131st 135th and 152nd Reports: 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if 
the House is not in Sessi on, during the Session immediately following 
the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if 
the House is in Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, 
during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear 
days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should 
henceforth comply with this schedule in  the matter of laying of the 
Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha.” 
(131st Report) 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is 
essential that in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Order s, 
the concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay statement the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identifying bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135th Report) 

“In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned 
a distinctive number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, 
no notification should be published/laid which does not carry a 
notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in 
this regard. In case where there are more than one notification under a 
single file, the Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably distinguished from one 
another. 
(152nd Report)
