IV 
The Airports Authority of India (Lost Property) Regulations, 2003. 
            The Committee took up for examination the Airports Authority of India (Lost 
Property) Regulations, 2003 framed under the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994. A 
questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the 17th 
May, 2004 for their comments.  The Ministry furnished their comments vide O.M. 
dated the 6th October, 2004.  The points raised by the Committee and the comments of 
the Ministry thereon are as under:- 
(1)        (i)Point raised 
The Airports Authority of India (Lost Property) Regulations, 2003 have been framed in 
supersession of the IAAI (Lost Property) Regulation, 1974, the IAAI (Lost Property) 
(Amendment) Regulations, 1992 and the NAA (Lost Property) Regulations, 1988. 
  
                        Whether the Airports Authority of India (Lost Property) Regulations, 
2003 are the first set of regulations framed under the Airports Authority of India Act, 
1994, if so, in what manner, this area was being regulated in the absence of the said 
regulations.  
                        Ministry’s comments 
            These are the first set of regulations on the subject of Lost Property framed 
under the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994. Earlier the issue was governed by the 
two Gazette Notifications as under:- 
The International Airports Authority of India (Lost Property) Regulations, 1974. 
 The National Airports Authority (Lost Property) Regulations, 1988. 
The present Regulations superseded the aforesaid two Regulations. 
(ii) Point raised 
What necessitated the Government to bring in the regulations of 2003 in supersession of 
the earlier regulations as stated above and what are the major points of distinction 
between the regulations of 2003 and the earlier ones. 
 Ministry’s comments 
The Airports Authority of India was formed by Notification of AAI Act, 1994 and the 
IAAI Act, 1974 and NAA Act, 1988 were repealed.  Consequent on the notification of 
the appointed date of the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994, subordinate legislation 
in regard to framing of various regulations are required to be notified under Section 42 
of the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994.  In terms of section 42 sub-section 2 clause 
(f) of the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994, the Authority is required to frame 
regulations pertaining to lost property for all its airports.  Similar regulations were 
framed and notified by the erstwhile IAAI and NAA for the airports under its control 
before they were merged. 
Major points of distinction between the regulations of  2003 and the earlier ones are at 
Annexure. 
(2)        Point raised 
            As per regulation 2(j), ‘Officer’ means an officer of the authority other than the 
Airport Director or Incharge of the Airport or Civil Enclave. 

            As an ‘officer’ under the regulations is required to discharge functions involving 
a lot of responsibility, would it not be appropriate if a minimum level of the officer is 
indicated in the definition for the purpose of these regulations.  
            Ministry’s comments 
            Suggestions of the Committee have been noted.  The word ‘officer’ is being 
replaced with the Duty Airport Manager/Duty Officer Control Tower as the case may 
be’. A suitable amendment to this effect in the Airports Authority of India (Lost 
Property) Regulations, 2003 is being proposed. 
(3)        Point raised 
As per regulation 3, the officer to whom any lost property has been handed over is 
required to maintain a register containing the description of the lost property and the 
name, address and signatures of the person etc. However, as per regulation 4, the officer 
to whom the lost property has been handed over is required to pass on the same to the 
Lost Property Office within 24 hours and in case the property is handed over to the 
claimant in the meantime, the officer is required to report the facts and give the name, 
address and description of the lost property to the Lost Property Office. 
            Do the regulations not contemplate maintenance of records at two places one 
with the officer under regulation 3 and the other in the lost property office under 
regulation 4; is there any scope for streamlining the provisions further. 
             
            Ministry’s comments 
            The Lost Property Office under Regulation 4 functions from 0930 to 1730 hrs on 
normal working days and therefore, will be closed after office hours and on 
holidays.  His office is located away from the passenger terminal building.  The officer 
mentioned under Regulation 3 i.e. the Duty Airport Manager/Duty Officer Control 
Tower, is available round the clock subject to watch hours of the airport and any 
person finding the lost property can deposit the same with the Duty Airport 
Manager/Duty Officer Control Tower as the case may be.  
Claimant can claim the property from the Duty Airport Manager/Duty Officer Control 
Tower as the case may be, on round the clock basis subject to watch hours of the airport 
before it is deposited in the Lost Property Office. After the Lost Property is deposited 
with the Lost Property Officer, the claimant can claim the lost property from his office. 
            Therefore, in view of above, records of lost property are required to be 
maintained at both the places. 
(4)        Point raised  
            Regulation 6 deals with handing over of lost property to the claimant  
            What is normally the time taken for restoring property to the rightful claimant 
would it not be more appropriate if some maximum time period is prescribed so that 
the lost properties do not pile up in the Lost Property Office? 
            Ministry’s comments 
            The lost and found property is handed over to the rightful claimant immediately 
after the claimant proves the claim to the Duty Airport Manager/Duty Officer Control 
Tower, in-charge of the Airport of Civil Enclave.  In case no claim is received, the 
property is retained for three months and thereafter, disposal action is initiated as per 
the laid down procedure.  As such, to avoid piling up of lost property, the time limit is 
taken care. 
(5)        Point raised 
            As per regulation 7, in case the incharge of the Airport or the Civil Enclave is 
unable to secure a reasonable price, he is required to report the mater to the superior 
authority for suitable orders. 
  

            Is it not possible to prescribe some time schedule for action under regulation 
7(1)? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
            As the disposal action is to undergo the process of assessment by an approved 
valuer, notification for disposal, etc., it is generally done once in a year or on 
accumulation of substantial quantity to make the process economically viable, 
whichever is earlier.  In case any item fails to secure reasonable price it is included in 
the future disposal action after reviewing the reserve price, if necessary.  Considering 
the above, it may not be possible to prescribe a time schedule for action under 
regulation 7(1). 
(6)        Point raised 
            As per regulation 7 (4), a person whose property has been disposed of is entitled 
to receive the proceeds of the same after deduction of reasonable expenses, which may 
not exceed 25 per cent of the same proceeds. 
            25 per cent of the sale proceeds does not seem to constitute reasonable expenses 
within the meaning of regulation 7 (4).  In what manner, Government have prescribed 
this time limit of 25 per cent and whether the same is  not on the higher side? 
            Ministry’s comments 
            Airports Authority of India incurs considerable expenditure towards carrying 
inventory for more than three months, assessment by an approved valuer, 
administrative cost on disposal, notification and conducting disposal by 
auction.  Airports Authority of India does not charge any expenses for handling the lost 
property in case it is handed over to the original claimant within three months.  Once 
the lost property is auctioned off after three months, a maximum of 25 per cent of sale 
proceed is deducted and the balance is given back to the owner on claim.  However, 25 
per cent is the upper limit and the actual amount recovered could be less than 25 per 
cent depending on the value of the lost property.  In view of above, it is considered that 
percentage specified is justified. 
  
(7)        Point raised 
  
            The regulations are silent about compensating the claimant/rightful owner of 
property in deserving cases; how and where this aspect of the matter has been dealt 
with? 
            Ministry’s comments 
            The regulation is dealing with lost and found property only.  The claimant is 
either given back the property or paid the proceeds of the sale after deducting 
reasonable expenses not exceeding 25 per cent of the sale proceeds. The Airports 
Authority of India is not responsible for any lost property, which has not been handed 
over to the Airports Authority of India. 
2.         The replies of the Ministry were considered by the Committee on the 17th 
November, 2005. The Committee noted that the Ministry had agreed to replace the 
words “any officer” occurring at a number of places in the Airports Authority of India 
(Lost Property) Regulations, 2003 with the words “Duty Airport manager/Duty Officer 
Control Tower as the case may be”. However, with regard to regulation 6 
the  Committee desired that the Ministry should prescribe a time limit in the regulation 
itself to make it unambiguous and also to ensure that the lost property, if claimed, is 
restored to the rightful claimant within a stipulated time period. The Ministry vide their 
O.M. dated the 21st February, 2006 clarified as under:- 
            “ Attention of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation may  be drawn to 
Regulation 7 (1) of the Airports Authority of India (Lost Property) Regulations, 2003, 

wherein a time period of three months  for restoring the lost property to the claimant 
has already been prescribed.” 
            The Committee, thereafter, accepted the clarification of the Ministry. 
            The Committee notes that the Ministry have agreed to notify amendments in 
regulations 3 (1) and (2) and regulation 4 by substituting the words “any officer” with 
the words “ Duty Airport Manager/ Duty Officer Control Tower as the case may be” as 
suggested by the Committee. The Committee hopes that the Ministry shall notify the 
amendment expeditiously.  
V 
The Export-Import Bank of India General Regulations, 1982 
  
            The EXIM Bank of India General Regulations, 1982 framed under the EXIM 
Bank of India Act, 1981 were examined and certain points were referred to the Ministry 
of Finance on the 7th June, 1995 for their comments. 
The Committee discussed the subject matter with the representatives of the EXIM Bank 
and the Ministry of Finance at Mumbai on the 21st June, 1995.  During the discussions, 
the Committee observed that the EXIM Bank of India Act, 1981 gives full powers to the 
Board but the provisions of regulation 10 (i) and (ii) have reduced the powers of the 
Board thus making this body redundant.  It desired that the regulations be reviewed as 
the Managing Committee constituted by the Board was usurping the powers of the 
Board.  The Committee also desired reviewing of regulation 6.  
The subject matter was again discussed with the representatives of the EXIM Bank and 
the Ministry of Finance at Mumbai on the 18th January, 1996.  The Committee 
reiterated its earlier views on regulations 6 and 10 that these be reviewed and amended 
as suggested by it.  
The Ministry of Finance (Banking Division) vide their communication dated the 12th 
September, 1996 stated that regulation 6 dealing with disclosure of interest by a 
Director of the EXIM Bank is in conformity with the General Regulations of other 
institutions and therefore, it was not necessary to carry out proposed amendment in 
regulation 6 and the Government also agreed with this view.  Regarding regulation 10, 
it has been stated that in compliance of the Committee’s direction the Ministry have 
suggested the EXIM Bank to effect changes in this regulation. 
Thereafter, the matter was placed before the Committee in its meeting held on the 15th 
May, 1998.  The Committee observed that it was not known whether the proposed 
amendments in regulations 3, 5 and 7 approved by the Board, have been notified or not 
and directed the Ministry to let it know if the notifications have been issued. On 
regulations 6 & 10 the Committee reiterated its earlier views on the matter. 
  
Its communication dated the 15th November 2000 the Ministry sought extension of time 
up to the 31st December, 2000 to comply with the Committee’s observations. The matter 
was then fervently pursued with constant reminders to the Ministry. In its 
communication dated the 25th February, 2002 the Ministry informed the Committee 
that its suggestions on regulation 6 have been examined in consultation with the EXIM 
Bank and it is not unusual for a Director to hold a minimum marketable lot of 100 
shares.  The acceptance of the Committee’s suggestion may pose practical difficulties in 
the matter.  In respect of regulation 10, it has been stated that the same is being 
examined in consultation with the Bank.  Thereafter, the Ministry sought extension of 
time up to the 31st March, 2002, which was later on, on the Ministry’s request, further 
extended till 31st December 2002.   
The Ministry vide their communication dated the 1st January, 2003 informed the 
Committee that the amendments to regulations 3(i), 3(iv), 3(vii), 5(i), 7(2) and 7(3) have 
been notified vide Gazette notification G.S.R. 1/2002 dated the 9th February, 2002 

(Annexure-I).  However, implementation of the Committee’s suggestion on regulation 
10 was still pending and the Ministry sought extension of time upto the 30th November, 
2003. 
The points raised in the questionnaire the Ministry’s comments thereon, Committee’s 
further observations and the Ministry’s comments thereto alongwith the Action Taken 
by the Ministry are as follows:- 
1.         Point referred: 
The Regulations under examination do not clearly and precisely specify the powers and 
the functions of the Chairman or Managing Director and other Members of the 
Board?  Whether the Regulations are proposed to be modified, accordingly. 
  
Ministry’s reply (21.6.95) 
In terms of Section 10(ii) of the General Regulations, the Chairman, if he is a whole time 
director or the Managing Director, is authorised to have full powers to do all the things 
required to be done by Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank) except to the extent 
provided in Section 10(i) of the General Regulations, which can be exercised only by the 
Board.  The powers of the Chairman or the Managing Director have also been 
described in Sections 10(ii), 11, 12(i) of the General Regulation. 
            Also, the Export-Import Bank of India Act in terms of Section 5(2) provides as 
follows: 
            “Save as otherwise provided in the regulations made under this Act- 
The Chairman, if he is a whole-time director or if he is holding offices both as the 
Chairman and the Managing Director, or  
The Managing Director, if the Chairman is not a whole time director, or, if the 
Chairman being a whole-time director, is absent, 
shall also have powers of general superintendence, direction and management of the 
affairs and business of the EXIM Bank and may also exercise all powers and do all acts 
and things which may be exercised or done by the EXIM Bank.” 
            As regards the powers of the Board, the Export-Import Bank of India Act, in 
terms of Section 5(1) provides as under: 
The general superintendence, direction and management of the affairs and business of 
the EXIM Bank shall vest in the Board, which may exercise all powers and do all acts 
and things which may be exercised or done by the EXIM Bank.” 
In view of the above, we do not propose to modify the Regulation. 
Committee’s observation :(21.6.95) 
The Committee felt that this provision requires reconsideration.  The Committee 
directed that a meeting with the Chairman of the Bank and the Ministry of Finance be 
fixed at Delhi, to chalk this out. 
Ministry’s further reply :(18.1.96) 
  
Relevant data from regulations of other financial institutions has been compiled and 
submitted to the Banking Division.  Provision similar to Regulation 10(i) of EXIM 
Bank’s General Regulations has been found in Regulation 11 of Industrial 
Reconstruction Bank of India’s General Regulations.  While in terms of Section 5(i) of 
the Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981, the Board may exercise all powers and do 
all acts and things which may be exercised or done by EXIM Bank, the Management 
Committee has been given powers under Regulation 4(i) to transact all the usual 
business of EXIM Bank except the powers enumerated under Regulation 10(i) which 
have been specifically reserved only to the Board.  Besides, decisions taken by the 
Management Committee are reported to the Board at the following meeting.  Thus the 
supremacy of the Board is not affected in any manner. 
            Committee’s observation:(18.1.96)  

The Chairman of the Committee pointed out that these Regulations were last 
considered on 21st June, 1995 in Mumbai itself and the Committee then pointed out that 
the EXIM Bank of India Act, 1981 had given full powers to the Board but the 
Regulation 10(i) of the Bank had curtailed the powers of the Board to mere approval of 
balance sheet etc.  On the contrary, the Managing Committee, which should have been 
otherwise answerable to the Board, being the creation of the Board, itself has become 
more powerful than the Board.  The regulation has, therefore, gone beyond than what is 
permitted by the Parent Act i.e. the EXIM Bank of India Act, 1981.  The Committee on 
the previous occasion in June 1995 had directed the Bank and the Ministry of Finance 
to remove the anomaly by suitably amending the regulation. 
            The Committee was not satisfied with the reply tendered by the EXIM Bank and 
was of the view that the Bank has attempted to justify the existence of this regulation, 
i.e., Regulation 10(i) by citing similar provisions from other financial institutions such 
as IRBI etc.  The Committee opined that regulations can not and shall not override the 
Parent Act which has delegated the power to the Bank. 
            The Committee directed that the regulation may be suitably amended according 
to the letter and spirit of the Parent Act and the Committee may be informed about the 
proposed amendment within a reasonable period of time.  The Chairman of the EXIM 
Bank agreed to it and assured that the earlier matter including the observations made 
by the Committee in June, 1995 regarding Regulations 3(i), (iii), (vii), 5(i), 6 and 7(2), 
would be placed before the Board at its next meeting which is likely to be held in March, 
1996 and a decision would be taken on the issues. 
2.         Point referred: Regulation 3(i) 
“Meetings of the Board shall be convened by the Chairman or the Managing Director 
or, in their absence, by an Executive Director of the EXIM Bank nominated by the 
Chairman or Managing Director in this behalf, at least four times in each calendar year 
and at least once in each quarter.” 
Whether the Ministry have any objection, if the words ‘at least once in each quarter’ 
are substituted by ‘at least once in every three months’? 
Ministry’s reply (21.6.95) 
As the quarter also relates to a three-month period in a calendar year, the submission is 
that the word  ‘quarter’ may be retained. 
Committee’s observations (21.6.95) 
The Committee directed that this regulation be made more specific by inserting words 
“at least once in every three months” instead of “once in each quarter”.  The Chairman 
and the Managing Director of the Bank agreed to the proposal. 
Ministry’s Further reply (18.1.96) 
            The proposal would be placed before the Board for approval of the suggested 
amendment, in consultation with Banking Division. 
Action Taken by the Ministry (1.1.2003) 
The Ministry have notified the amendment as suggested by the Committee. 
Point referred: Regulation 3(iii), 5(i) and 7(2) 
Regulation 3(iii), 5(i) and 7(2) provide that the meetings of the Board, Management 
Committee and other meetings of the Board, Management Committee and other 
Committees respectively shall be held at the Head Office of the EXIM Bank, or at such 
other place in India as may be specified in the notice convening the meeting. 
What is the justification for providing for convening meetings outside the Head Office 
of the EXIM Bank?  Whether the Ministry have any objection in limiting the number of 
Meetings? 
Ministry’s reply (21.6.95) 
Board meetings have so far been held only in Delhi and Mumbai, except one meeting in 
Kolkata in 1983  and one in Chennai in 1984.  All Management Committee Meetings 

have been held only in Mumbai, except three meetings in 1982 and one in 1983, which 
were held in Delhi. 
No criteria have been laid down for convening meetings of the Board or the 
Management Committee outside the Head office of EXIM Bank. 
            The Regulations prescribe the minimum number of meetings to be convened in a 
calendar year.  The Bank is a specialized financial institution dealing with international 
trade and finance, where competition is from overseas and as such, time is of essence in 
decisions.  Occasions could arise to convene emergency meetings of the Board or the 
Management Committee to take urgent decisions causing total number of meetings to 
exceed the minimum number of meetings prescribed in the Regulations. 
            Submission is that limiting the number of meetings in a calendar year or 
restricting holding a meeting at any other important commercial place, will deprive the 
Bank of the above flexibility in terms of convening emergency meetings for transacting 
urgent business. 
Committee’s observation (21.6.95) 
  
The Committee accepted the version given by the Bank. 
  
4.         Point referred: Regulations 3(iv), 5(i) and 7(2) 
Regulations 3(iv), 5(i) and 7(2) provide that sufficient notice shall be given to every 
Director for Meeting of Board, Managing Committee and Other Committees. 
The term ‘sufficient notice’ appearing in the Regulations is vague.  Whether the 
Ministry have any objection in specifying a minimum time limit for convening an 
emergency meeting of the Board, meeting of the Management Committee and the 
meeting of other Committees. 
Ministry’s reply (21.6.95) 
The term ‘sufficient notice’ is taken to reflect any notice period shorter than two weeks, 
which has concurrence of director attending a meeting.  In view of this, the submission 
is that a minimum time limit for convening an emergency meeting of the Board, meeting 
of the Management Committee may not be prescribed. 
Committee’s observation (21.6.95) 
The Committee directed that for emergent meetings a notice of 3 days would suffice.  A 
saving clause may be inserted “that under emergent conditions, the Chairman will act 
on behalf of the Board and report the same to the Board in the next meeting.” 
            Ministry’s further reply (18.1.96) 
The proposal would be placed before the Board for approval of the suggested 
amendment, in consultation with Banking Division. 
Action Taken by the Ministry (1.1.2003) 
The Ministry have notified the amendment as suggested by the Committee. 
5.         Point referred 
Regulation 3(vi), 5(ii) and 7(3) provide for Quorum for the Meeting of Board, 
Management Committee and the other Committees.  It, however, does not govern the 
contingencies where the Quorum is not made out.  What is the fate of the meeting where 
adequate number of members to constitute the Quorum is not present pursuant to the 
notice? 
Ministry’s reply (21.6.95) 
  
If the Quorum is not made out at a meeting, no business will be transacted at such a 
meeting.  However, the meeting is deemed to have been convened as per 
Regulations.  So far, EXIM Bank has faced no difficulty regarding Quorum except in 
one case of a Board meeting in March 1991, as meetings are convened after ascertaining 
directors’ convenience and co-coordinating such convenience ensures a Quorum. 

Committee’s observation (21.9.95) 
The Committee accepted the comments of the Bank and decided not to proceed further 
in the matter.

 Action Taken by the Ministry:(1.1.03)

 (ii)       There has been no occasion so far warranting removal of a Director of the

A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN

REPORT 
I 

The Oil Mines Regulations, 1984 – Implementation of the 119th Report   of the 
Committee on  
Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha 
  
            The Committee presented its 119 th Report on the Oil Mines Regulat ions, 1984 to 
the House on the 10th July, 1998. A copy of the Report was forwarded to the Ministry of 
Petroleum & Natural Gas on the 14th July, 1998 for furnishing the Action Taken Report 
(ATR) thereon. A major recommendation of the Committee was the setting up of a multi-
member omnibus authority under an Act of Parliament, which may be known as the 
Hydrocarbons Authority of India, for overseeing the entire upstream hydrocarbons 
sector in the offshore areas, including safety of installations, health safety, and welfare of 
workers and environmental aspects. Relevant extracts from the said report are enclosed 
(Annexure). 
  
2.         The Ministry vide their letter dated the 6 th August, 1998 informed that the ATR 
was to be prepared in consultation with other Ministries for which a further additional 
period of six weeks was requested for submission of the ATR. In another communication 
dated the 14 th October, 1998 the Ministry sought further extension of time till the 31 st 
December, 1998 as they were engag ed in studying models on which the proposed 
Hydrocarbons Development Authority was to be based, as existing in countries like UK, 
Norway, Canada, U.S.A etc. 
  
3.         Thereafter, the Ministry had been seeking extension of time for furnishing the 
ATR. Subsequently, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas vide their letter dated 
the 9 th May, 2000 informed the constitution of an Inter - Ministerial Working Group 
headed by Shri Naresh Narad, the then Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Petroleum 
and Natural Gas, for studying the upstream Regulatory Authority. The Working Group 
was expected to submit its report by the 15th June, 2000 and the same was to be examined 
in the Ministry. The Committee had then observed that the Ministry's pace of 
implementing the Committee's recommendation was extremely slow. It also pointed out 
that it was a matter of serious concern that there was neither any statutory authority in 
position nor any statutory rules/regulations in place for overseeing the offshore activities 
while the work of offering new blocks in the offshore basins was already on. It felt that 
the Ministry had failed to take note of the urgency emphasized by the Committee thereby 
rendering the Committee's whole exercise redundant. 
  
4.         The Committee heard the Secretary, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas in 
the matter on the 17 th July, 2001. During the course of the meeting, the Committee was 
informed that the report of the Working Group, since submitted to the ministry on the 
4th April, 2001, was under consideration of the Ministry and a decision in the matter 
would be taken up after the same was examined. This would be followed by approval of 
the Cabinet. The Ministry had also stated that, in their view, there should be one 
upstream regulatory authority. 
  
5.         Thereafter, the Ministry had sought extension of time on a number of occasions, 
i.e. upto 30.11.2001, 28.2.02 and 31.5.02 for furnishing the ATN on the plea that the report 
submitted by the Working Group was still under examination. Th e Ministry was 
requested to furnish a detailed note specifically commenting on the extent to which each 
recommendation of the Committee, as contained in its 119 th report was acceptable to 
them, the action so far taken by them towards implementing the same and a definite time 
span within which they would be able to implement the Committee's recommendations. 
On the 8 th August, 2002 the Ministry informed that the Government had initiated the 

process for dismantling the Administered Price Mechanism after March 2002 and to put 
into place a Regulatory Authority for the Downstream Petroleum sector. In view of these 
developments, it had decided to process the recommendations of the Working Group on 
upstream sector. They had also contended that the proposal of the Working Group would 
also require inter-Ministerial/Departmental consultation which might took a few months 
more. Accordingly, the Ministry requested for further extension of time upto the 31 st 
October, 2002 for furnishing the ATR on the matter. On the same g round, the Ministry 
sought repeated extension of time, i.e. up to 31.01.03, 30.4.03 and 31.7.03 
  
6.      The Committee in its meeting held on the 31 st March, 2003 decided to call the 
concerned Joint Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas to appear before the 
Chairman of the Committee, and a meeting was arranged on 25th July, 2003. Afterwards, 
the Ministry vide its communication dated the 1 st August, 2003 sought extension of time 
up to the 31 st March, 2004 to furnish the Action Taken Report, as the report of the 
Working Group was being considered in light of the progress and developments on 
dismantling of the Administered Price Mechanism and formation of regulatory 
mechanism for the downstream sector. They further submitted that the formation of 
Regulatory Mechanism for Upstream Hydrocarbons sector could be taken up only after 
such Regulatory frameworks for downstream Hydrocarbons sector has been put in place. 
  
7.         The Ministry vide  its letter dated the 14 th May, 2004 sought further extension of 
time upto the 31st August, 2004 for furnishing the ATR,  as a bill introduced in Parliament 
incorporating the report of the Working Group could not be effected/materialized  as Lok 
Sabha was yet to be formed and the bill could be t aken up after the constitution of Lok 
Sabha. Again, the Ministry vide its letter dated the 2nd September, 2004 sought extension 
of time upto the 28 th February, 2005 on the ground that the bill for establishing a 
Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (for downstream sector) introduced in Lok 
Sabha on the 18th December, 2003 could not be taken up by the House in that session, and 
the new Government also decided that the new draft Bill should incorporate provisions 
relating to a Technical Body to advice o n technical issues as also an Appellate Tribunal. 
The Ministry contemplated to introduce the Bill for Regulatory Board for downstream 
sector in the winter session of Parliament. 
  
8.         Thereafter, several reminders were issued to the Ministry to furnish the     ATR. 
  
9.         Finally, the Ministry in its communication dated the 10th June, 2005 informed as 
under: - 
  
 “For the present, Govt. of India is not contemplating a separate and independent 
regulator for the up-stream sector”. 
  
10.       Thereafter, the Ministry were requested to furnish a detailed background note 
on the basis of which their latest decision was arrived at. 
  
11.       The Ministry vide its latest communication dated the 18th July, 2005 informed as 
under: - 
  
“The main recommendation of the Committee was to set up “Hydrocarbon Authority of 
India” in the country on the pattern followed by UK, Norway, Canada and USA for 
overseeing the entire upstream sector in the offshore areas. The recommendation of the 
committee was examined i n the Ministry, and since it required in depth study, it was 
considered appropriate to constitute a high -powered Inter-Ministerial Working Group 

to go into various aspects. The Working Group submitted its report, which was examined 
in the Ministry as well as by the Committee of Secretaries headed by the Cabinet 
Secretary. 
  
            After deliberation in detail, it has been decided not to have, for the present, a 
separate and independent regulator for the upstream sector for following reasons: 
  
Petroleum & Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) when formed would regulate the 
petroleum operations beyond the crude oil and natural gas production phase covering 
refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing and sale of 
petroleum and petroleum products as well as natural gas and its transportation through 
pipelines. PNGRB, would also regulate the establishment of LNG terminals and setting 
up of city or local gas distribution projects. The upstream sector is distinct from the 
downstream se ctor and has different business clientele and technical issues of a 
completely different scope and nature, apart from entailing higher risk investments. With 
the exception of Brazil, the activities of upstream sector elsewhere are generally 
controlled and regulated by the Governments themselves. 
  
As the ownership of the resources in the upstream sector is vested with the Government, 
it would be desirable and appropriate for the Government, with the help of Director -
General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) to regulate  upstream activity under Oilfields 
(Regulation and Development) Act, 1948. This act provides the legal framework for 
regulating the upstream sector.   The New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) for 
awarding blocks for exploration and production provides th e fiscal regime, manner of 
selection of parties and the modalities for Production Sharing contracts. DGH had been 
set up for advising the Government on technical matters like reservoir management, data 
management etc. The Ministry is of the view that the present policy and regulation regime 
for the upstream sector is adequate and DGH would regulate the upstream Hydrocarbon 
sector while the PNGRB would regulate the Downstream Hydrocarbon sector, once 
PNGRB is formed.   In view of this, the Govt. is not contem plating a separate and 
independent regulator for upstream hydrocarbon sector for the present.” 
  
The Committee considered the matter in the light of the latest information furnished by 
the Ministry. After a holistic review of the matter, the Committee note d that since the 
beginning, when the Ministry was first approached to furnish the ATR on its 
recommendations as contained in its 119th Report, the Ministry had been maintaining the 
position that an upstream regulatory authority was desirable for the upstre am 
hydrocarbon sector. The Committee was given to understand that the matter was being 
examined and an Inter -Ministerial Working Group have been set up to look into the 
matter.The Committee was approached on numerous occasions for granting extension of 
time as the report of the Working Group was under deliberation in the Ministry and, 
subsequently it was to be followed by approval of the Cabinet. While going through the 
latest information furnished by the Ministry, which in essence amounted to the Ministry 
backtracking on their earlier position on the matter which they had endorsed so many 
times.  The Committee accepts the explanation furnished by the Ministry, but at the same 
time note with regret that it should not have allowed so much time to elapse in ar riving 
at the final decision.

The Rules Framed under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 – 
Implementation of the  
151st Report of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation,  Rajya Sabha.

framed under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999:- 
  
The Foreign Exchange Management (Encashment of Drafts, Cheque Instrument &

The Foreign Exchange Management (Adjudication, Proceedings & Appeal) Rules, 2000; 
and 
  
The Foreign Exchange Management (Compounding Proceedings) Rules, 2000. 
  
 In the said report, the Committee had recommended as follows: 
  
“ The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Finance have accepted the 
Committee’s suggestions as follows: 
  
On Rule 4 of FEM (Encashment of Drafts, Cheque   Instrument & Payment of Interest) 
Rules, 2000 to prescribe a definite time frame for encashing th e draft, cheques, etc. and 
as a follow up, would be requesting the RBI to issue suitable instructions to the Banks in 
this behalf. 
  
To take necessary action to do away with the inconsistency in Schedules I   & II of FEM 
(Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000,by inserting an introductory portion in the 
English version also. 
  
(a) To delete the word “brief’ in Rule 4(9) of the FEM (Adjudication, Proceedings & 
Appeal) Rules, 2000. The Committee had objected to the provision whereby the decision 
of the Adjudicating Authority was prescribed to contain “brief reasons for the decisions”. 
  
(b) To prescribe a time limit of 180 days in Rule 6(4) of the FEM (Adjudication, 
Proceedings & Appeal) Rules, 2000 for disposal of appeals. The rules at present do not 
prescribe any time period for disposal of appeals, which was objected to by the

            The Committee hopes that the Ministry would notify amendments in the respective

III 
The Railway Claims Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1989 – Implementation of 
 123rd Report of the Committee. 
  
The Railway Claims Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1989 framed under the Railways 
Claims Tribunal Act, 1989 were examined by the Committee and the matter was reported 
to the House on the 21 st December, 1998 in its 123 rd Report wherein the Committee had 
recommended as under : - 
            “The Committee considered the subject at its meeting held on September 8, 1998 
and noted the comments of the Ministry of Railways in respect of Rules 17, 27 (2) and (3), 
30 and 33.   As regards the rules 11(3), 22, 32(2) and 3 1(1), the Committee noted with 
satisfaction that the Ministry had accepted its suggestion.  The Committee expressed the 
desire that the Ministry of Railways should carry out necessary amendment to the 
relevant rules, where Committees’ suggestion have been accepted expeditiously.” (para 
4.4) 
  
2.         Relevant extracts from the 123 rd Report were forwarded to the Ministry of 
Railways (Railway Board) on the 22 nd April, 1999 for implementation of its 
recommendations. 
  
3. The Ministry of Railways vide their communication dated the 21 st November, 2000 
informed as under: 
“The recommendation of the Committee to change Rules 11(3), 22, 31(1) and 32(2) have 
been examined in consultation with the Legislative Department of the Ministry of Law 
and Justice. 
            Legislative Department opined that the proposed amendments in Rule 11(3) & 22 
relating to removal of defects in the application before Registrar and the summoning of 
witnesses by the Tribunal recording the reasons in writing, are free from any legal 
difficulties.  The same can be carried out. 
  
The amendment proposed in Rule 31(1) relates to passing of an order either at once or as 
soon as thereafter but not later than 30 days from the date of conclusion of evidence and 
arguments.  The amendment prescribing the time limit of 30 days imposes a bar on the 
exercise of jurisdiction, and therefore would be outside the scope of the Act. 
            Regarding Rule 32(2) it has been opined that when Review is not provided by the 
substantive Act, it cannot be provided by means of Rule.  The provision of appeal, review 
or revision are made by the substantive Act and it relates to the jurisdiction and powers 
of a Tribunal.   Rules cannot provide appeal or review if it is not provided by the 
substantive Act. 
             
Rule 11(3) & Rule 22  are being amended as suggested by the Committee.   In so far as 
Rules 31(1) & 32(2)  are concerned, the Committee may like to reconsider the proposed 
amendments in view of the aforesaid legal implications and advise.”             
4.         The Committee considered the matter at its meeting held on the 16 th September, 
2004.  The Committee noted that the Ministry of Railways have implemented all the 
recommendations of the Committee as contained in its 123 rd Report on the Railway 
Claims ( Procedure) Rules, 1989 except those relating to rules 31(1) and 32(2).   The 
Committee was not convinced with the explanation furnished by the Ministry for their 
inability to implement its recommendations and decided to pursue the matter with the 
Ministry. 

5.         Accordingly, vide this Secretariat O.M. dated the 8 th October, 2004, the Ministry 
of Railways were requested to reconsider their stand on the Committee’s 
recommendations on these two rules in the light of the provisions of the Railway Claims 
Tribunal Act. 
6.         The Ministry of Railways vide their communication dated the 24 th March, 2005 
informed that the amendments to Rules 31(1) and 32(2) had since been notified vide 
  
G.S.R 173 (E) dated the 16 th March, 2005 publishing the Railway Claims T ribunal 
(Procedure) Amendment Rules, 2005. 
  
7.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Railways have 
amended the rules as per its suggestions as follows: - 
(i) Rule 11(3)    by providing that if on scrutiny an application, is fo und defective and 
defect noticed is formal in nature, the Registrar may allow the applicant to rectify the 
same in his presence, and if the defect is not formal in nature, the Registrar may allow 
the applicant to rectify defect in a week’s time, which may be extended in appropriate 
cases on the written request of the applicant. 
 
(ii) Rule 22(1)   by providing that if an application is presented by any party to the 
proceedings for summoning of witness, the Tribunal shall issue summons for the 
appearance of such witness by recording the reasons for doing so, unless it considers that 
the appearance of the witness is not necessary for the just decision of the case. 
 
(iii) Rule 31(1)   by substituting that the Tribunal, after hearing the applicant and 
respondent, shall pass an order either at once, or as soon as thereafter, as may be 
practicable but not later than twenty -one days from the date of conclusion of the 
arguments; and where is it unable to do so, it shall record its reasons for such inability; 
and  
 
(iv) Rule 32(2)   by substituting that where it appears to the Tribunal that there is no 
sufficient ground for a review, it shall reject the application and record its reasons for so 
doing.

IV 
  
The Railways (Opening for Public Carriage of  Passengers)    Rules, 2000-
Implementation 
 of 149th Report of the Committee. 
  
The Railways (Opening for Public Carriage of Passengers) Rules, 2000 were included in 
the 149th Report of the Committee presented to the House on the 19 th August, 2003. The 
Committee in the 149th Report had recommended as under: 
  
"The Committee considered the comments of the Ministry on the questionnaire at its 
meetings held on the 7 th May, 2003. The  Committee notes with satisfaction that the 
Ministry of Railways have accepted the Committee's suggestions on (i) Rule 19 
Explanation to modify the provision so as to specify the documents or types of documents 
required to be forwarded to the Commissioner for initiation of electric traction on a line; 
and (ii) Rule 24(5) to substitute the words "earliest opportunity" with suitable words so 
as to specify that the action is taken within a time frame between period of initiation of 
diversion and use of such temporary diversion to ensure prompt action on the part of the 

Commissioner. The Committee however, recommends that Rule 24(4) may be amended 
by substituting the words "responsible officer" with the words "Railway servant in 
charge of the work" in view of th eir comments. The Committee hopes that the Ministry 
would carry out these amendments expeditiously under intimation to it". 
  
2.         Relevant extracts from the 149 th Report were forwarded to the Ministry of 
Railways for necessary action on the 22 nd August, 2003. The Ministry vide their 
communication dated the 24 th May, 2004 furnished Action Taken Note on Rules 24 (4) 
and 24(5). The Committee considered the matter at its meeting held on the 7 th January, 
2005. The points referred to the Ministry, their co mments received thereon and the 
observations of the Committee are reproduced below:- 
  
I           POINT REFERRED 
  
Rule 24 (4) regarding substitution of the words "responsible officer" with the words 
"Railway servant in charge of the work." 
  
            Ministry's reply 
  
            The suggestion made by the Committee in their last para regarding Rule 24 (4) 
has been accepted by the Ministry of Railways and the same has been sent along with 
other necessary amendments to the said rules to Ministry of Law , Justice and Company 
Affairs (Legal Section) for their legal vetting so that the said rules can be published in the 
gazette. The proposed amendments are still under correspondence with the legal Ministry 
and the issue is likely to be sorted out soon. 
  
Committee’s observations (7.1.2005) 
  
            The Committee noted that the Ministry are taking necessary action with regard to 
making changes in rule 24 (4) in pursuance to its recommendations. 
  
II          POINT REFERRED 
  
Rule 24 (5) regarding substitution of the words 'earliest opportunity' with suitable 
words so as to specify that action is taken within a time frame between period of initiation 
of diversion and use of such temporary diversion to ensure prompt action on the part of 
the Commissioner. 
  
            Ministry's reply 
  
            So far as the recommendation of the Committee regarding Rule 24 (5) is 
concerned, Ministry has decided not to make any change. 
  
            Committee’s observations (7.1.2005) 
  
            The Committee was not satisfied with the comments of the Ministry on rule 24 
(5).  It took exception to the Ministry’s statement that they had “decided not to make any 
change” in rule 24 (5) and desired that the Ministry may be asked to furnish a detailed 
justification why the Committee’s recommendations in relation to rule 24 (5) are not 
acceptable to them.    
  

3.         Accordingly, a reference was sent to the Ministry on the 5 th May, 2005.   The 
Ministry of Railways furnished Action Taken Note on the 3 rd May, 2005.  The Ministry 
have amended and notified Rule 24 (4) as per the Committee’s suggestion by substituting 
the words “responsible officer” with the words “railway servant in-change of work”.  
  
            Regarding Rule 24(5), the Ministry have furnished a detailed note justifying  their 
non-acceptance of the Committee’s suggestion on the said rule which is reproduced 
below: 
  
            “The Committee’s recommendation as contained in its 149th Report in relation to 
Rule 24 (5) could not be agreed to particularly in view that the day safety of the running 
trains is the responsibility of the Ministry of Railways and not that of the 
Commissioner.  As can be seen from the Section 6 of the Railways Act, 1989, the duties of 
the Commissioner are as given below:- 
  
Inspect any railway with a view to determine whether it is fit to be opened for the public 
carriage of passengers and report thereon to the Central Government as required by or 
under this Act. 
  
Make such periodical or other inspections of any railw ay or of any rolling stock used 
thereon as the Central Government may direct. 
  
Make an inquiry under this Act into the cause of any accident on a railway.  
  
Discharge such other duties as are conferred on him by or under this Act.   
  
Therefore, keeping the above in view, the provision under Rule 24 (5) for inspection of 
the temporary diversion continuing for more than 3 days by the Commissioner has been 
kept as discretionary rather than making it mandatory.  Therefore, it has been stipulated 
in Rule 24(5) that Commissioner may inspect it at the “earliest opportunity” rather than 
fixing any definite time limit.  
  
It is hoped that the Committee would appreciate the view of the Railway Ministry”. 
  
In accordance to their explanation as given above, the Mini stry have amended and 
notified Rule 24(5) by substituting sub rule (5) of rule 24 so as to provide that “where the 
use of temporary diversion as likely to be extended to more than 3 days, the 
Commissioner shall, if he considers it necessary, take the earliest possible opportunity of 
inspecting it”. 
  
4.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Railways have since 
published the Railways (Opening for Public Carriage of Passengers) (Amendment) Rules, 
2005 vide notification No. G.S.R. 44(E) dated the 27 th January, 2005 (i) modifying the 
provisions of Rule 19  Explanation so as to provide that when sanction is required for the 
initiation of electric traction on a line already opened for passenger traffic, the documents 
specified in terms (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of sub rule (1), item (d) of sub rule (2) and item 
(a) (vii) of sub rule 5 shall be forwarded to the Commissioner; and (ii) in case of   rule 
24(4)  by substituting the words ‘responsible officer’ with the words ‘servant-in-charge’. 
Regarding Rule 24(5), the Committee accepts the explanation furnished by the Ministry 
of Railways for non -revision of the provisions of Rule 24(5) as suggested by it.   The 
Committee, however,  notes that as a follow up to their explanation, the Ministry have 
since amended Rule 24 (5) by providing that “where the use of temporary diversion is 

likely to be extended to more than 3 days the Commissioner shall, if he considers it 
necessary, take the earliest possible opportunity of inspecting it.”

V 
  
The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001. 
  
            The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules , 2001 framed 
under the Prevention of Cruelty to animals Act, 1960 were examined and a questionnaire 
on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of environment & Forests for their 
comments/clarifications on the 25 th November, 2003.   The Ministry furnished  their 
comments/clarifications on the 21st September, 2004.  The points referred to the Ministry 
and the comments/clarifications received thereon are reproduced below:- 
  
1          Point referred 
  
            The legislation under which these rules have been framed is of 1960.   In what 
manner the aspects covered by these rules were being regulated prior to framing of these 
rules? 
  
            Ministry comments 
  
            Prior to this legislation, the State governments/Local bodies formulated their own 
Rules and Regulations for functioning of the slaughter houses. 
  
II          Point referred 
            Rule 2 (c) Definition 
  
            “Slaughter house” means a slaughter house wherein 10   animals are slaughtered 
per day and is duly licensed or recognized under a Central, State or Provincial Act or any 
rules or regulations made thereunder”. 
  
            Are these rules applicable to such slaughter houses where less than 10 animals are 
slaughtered per day; why these have been excluded from the defini tion of “Slaughter 
House”? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            It may not be possible to depute so many veterinary officers to conduct the proper 
ant and post -mortem examination as the number of such places where animals are 
slaughtered in twos, threes, fours or even little more may be very high and at scattered 
places.  In addition to economic considerations, proper handling and disposal of slaughter 
wastes will be a problem.  Therefore, a minimum criterion of 10 animals to be slaughtered 
has been fixed to implement these Rules effectively and check the clandestine slaughter. 
  
III.       Point referred 
            Rule 4(2) Reception area or resting grounds 
  
            “The veterinary doctor shall examine thoroughly not more than 12 animals in an 
hour and not more than 96 animals in a day”. 
  

            Is it possible to examine 96 animals in a day which normally has eight working 
hours including lunch break? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            Depending on the species, time required for the examination varies.  The number 
specified is the maximum limit.   It is not mandatory for the veterinarian that he must 
examine 96 animals in a day. 
  
IV.       Point referred 
            Rule 4(3) Reception area or resting grounds. 
  
            “The veterinary doctor after examining the animal shall issue a fitness certificate 
in the form specified by the Central Government for this purpose”. 
  
            Whether Government h ave any objection in incorporating the format of fitness 
certificate in the rules itself? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            The format has to be in conformity with international/national requirements and 
therefore, this shall need modificatio n/amendments from time to time.   Hence not 
incorporated in the Rules itself. 
  
V.        Point referred 
            Rule 6(6) Slaughter  
  
            “A curbed -in bleeding area of adequate size as specified by the Central 
Government shall be provided in a  slaughter house and it shall be so located that the 
blood could not be splashed on other animals being slaughtered or on the carcass being 
skinned”. 
  
            What are the reasons that the Central Government have been authorized to 
specify the curbed -in bleeding area?   Does this size vary with the size of the Slaughter 
House and if so, can this function not be delegated to the State Governments or other 
local authority? 
  
            Ministry’s comments 
  
            The size of the slaughter house and species of the animals to be slaughtered shall 
govern the size of curbed -in bleeding area.   The implementing agencies are State 
Governments/Local bodies.   In order to maintain uniformity throughout the country, 
power has been vested with the Central Government.   
  
VI.       Point referred 
            Rule 9(1) Inspection of slaughter house  
  
            “The Animal Welfare Board of India or any person or Animal Welfare 
Organization authorized by it may inspect any slaughter house without notice to its owner 
or the person in charge of it at any time during the working hours to ensure that the 
provisions of these rules are being complied with”.  
  

What is the frequency of such inspections? Should the rules not prescribe a mini mum 
frequency of such inspections in every slaughter house so that the inspections are uniform 
and regular? 
The words ‘any person’ appear to be vague.  Whether Government have any objection in 
specifying the minimum level/status of such officer? 
  
Ministry’s comments 
  
The Government of India is agreeable to prescribe a minimum frequency of such 
inspections after working it out with the animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI), who are 
responsible for such inspections. 
  
The Government of India has no objection in specifying the minimum level/status of the 
inspecting officers in consultation with AWBI. 
  
2.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry have accepted its 
suggestions on point no. 6 on Rule 9(1) regarding inspection of slaughter h ouse to (i) 
prescribe a minimum frequency of inspection of slaughter houses so as to make such 
inspection uniform and regular; and (ii) to specify the minimum level/status of the 
inspecting officers.   On rest of the points, the committee accepts the Minist ry’s 
comments.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of environment & forests would carry 
out the amendments to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 
2001, expeditiously, under intimation to it.

2.         During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted 
some cases where there has been a considerable time lag between the date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where notifications have not been laid as per 
the Committee’s guidelines and whether such notifications were accompanied by 
a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the 
delay has been quite abnormal. The observations/recommendations of the 
Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: 
(i)       Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers  
          (Department of Chemicals& Petrochemicals) 
  
            The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 6 months in the laying 
of the only notification laid by the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers (Sl No. 5). 
The Ministry have appended a delay statement with the same. The Committee 
hopes that the Department of Chemical & Petrochemicals of the Ministry of 
Chemicals & Fertilizers would avoid such instances in future. 
  
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution  
            Department of Food & Public Distribution) 
  
The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 5 months in laying of one 
out of the five notifications laid by the Department of Food & Public Distribution 
of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (Sl No. 30). The 

Ministry have not appended a delay statement with the delayed notification.   The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Ministry of Consumer A ffairs, Food & 
Public Distribution would avoid such delays and would append a delay 
statement  in all such cases of delay in future. 
  
(iii)       Ministry of Finance  
(Department of Economic Affairs) 
  
The Committee notes that out of a total of   212 notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Finance (66 notifications by the Department of Economic Affairs and 
146 by the Department of Revenue) during the 207th Session, there is a delay in the 
laying of 2 notifications (Sl No. 39 & 44) by the Department of Economi c 
Affairs.  The Ministry have appended a delay statement with only one notification 
(Sl No. 44).  The reason for delay in laying the notification has been attributed to 
non receipt of the gazette copies from the Government of India Press by the Indian 
Bank.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance would avoid such 
instances in future.   The Committee also notes that the notification at Sl No. 97 
does not carry any distinctive number. In this context, the Committee would like 
to draw the Ministry’s attention towards its recommendation as contained in its 
152nd Report (relevant extracts reproduced later) whereby each notification must 
be allotted a distinctive number while notifying in the Gazette. The Committee 
hopes that the Ministry shall take care  of this aspect in future.    The Committee, 
however, appreciates that there is an overall decline in the instances of delay in 
the laying of notifications as compared to the position in earlier sessions and hopes 
that the Ministry of Finance would continue  with their efforts to avoid delay in 
laying of notifications and in case of any delay in their laying, shall keep the House 
informed of the reasons  for the same through delay statements. 
  
Ministry of Human Resource Development 
  
The Committee notes with  regret that the Ministry of Human Resource 
Development have delayed the laying of 3  notifications (Sl No. 269, 275 & 276) out 
of the 9 notifications laid by them.   While the Department of Elementary 
Education & Literacy have delayed the laying of one notification by 6 months, the 
Department of Secondary & Higher Education have delayed the laying of 2 of their 
notifications by 7 months and have also failed to append a delay statement.    The 
delay statement appended with the notification laid by the Departm ent of 
Elementary Education & Literacy (Sl No. 269) states the reason for delay as 
follows:- 
  
 “….The University notified the amendment on 1.8.2005 and got published the 
same in the Gazette of India Part III -Section IV on 20.8.2005.   Copies of the 
Gazette Notification were  sent by the University for laying on 10.10.2005.   These 
copies were received in the Ministry on 14.10.2005.  Copies duly authenticated by 
MOS (HRD) were received in the section on 16.12.2005.   This notification could 
not be laid in the Winter Session of Rajya Sabha due to the fact that the House 
was adjourned on 23.12.2005.” The Committee feel that the Ministry of Human 
Resource Development still had sufficient time to lay these notifications during the 
Winter Session 2005 if they had ac ted promptly.  The Committee recommends 
that Ministries should try to avail of the earliest opportunity to lay their papers 
before the Parliament rather than waiting for the later dates of the Session so as 
to avert eventualities like adjournment of the House pre mature.  The Committee 

also recommend the Ministry to invariably  append a delay statement  in all  cases 
of delay in future. 
  
(v)        Ministry of Labour & Employment 
  
The Committee is unhappy to note that out of the 4 notifications laid, the 
Ministry of Labour & Employment have delayed the laying of 2 of 
their  notifications (Sl No. 280 & 282).   Delay statement has been appended with 
both.  The delay statement for the laying of notification at Sl No. 280 states as 
under: 
  
“….at the time of la ying of the amendment incorporating a new Table ‘E’ and 
inclusion of para 39B after para  39A in the EPS, 1995 before Parliament, the Lok 
Sabha Secretariat pointed out that in all the amending rules, a footnote is required 
to be given at the end of the rul e containing therein the details of earlier 
amendments.  Thereafter, the Ministry inserted the requisite footnote by issuing a 
corrigendum to this effect and notifying the same in the Gazette on 16.8.2004, but 
a copy of the Gazette Notification was not rec eived in the Ministry.   Now the 
Notification has been obtained, which is why the delay.” 
  
The delay statement for the laying of notification at Sl No. 282 states, 
“…the copy of the Gazette Notification was received in the Ministry in February, 
2006, which is why the delay.” 
  
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Labour & Employment would 
take necessary corrective measures to avoid such instances in future. 
  
(vi)       Ministry of Power 
  
The Committee regrets to note that there is a delay of 6 months in laying of 
one out of the six notifications laid by the Ministry of Power (Sl No. 286). The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry of Power would avoid such instances in future. 
  
(vii)      Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions 
(Department of Personnel & Training) 
  
The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training) have laid 30 
notifications during the Session out of which 20 notifications (Sl No. 290-309) have 
been delayed.  While some notifications have been delayed by 6 -7 months, in 14 
cases there has been a delay of 1 year and 3 months. The Ministry have appended 
a delay statement with all the 20 delayed   notifications.  In their delay statement 
appended to the notifications, the Ministry have submitted as follows:- 
  
“The notification, which was sent to Government of India Press for 
publication in Part II Section 3 (i) of the Gazette of India on 12.9.2005, was 
published in the Extraordinary Gazette on 17.9.2005.  Due to administrative 
exigencies and frequent transfers of the officer dealing with the subject, the matter 
got delayed because the new incumbent needed time to acquaint himself with the 
procedure of publication, follow up with the Government of India Press for G.S.R. 
copies and laying down in both Houses of Parliament.   The delay in laying the 

notification in time is highly regretted.   This may be laid in both Houses of 
Parliament during the current session.” 
  
The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Personnel, Public 
Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training) could not avail of 
the opportunity to lay the subordinate legislation not only during the Budget 
Session-2005 but also during the Monsoon and Winter Sessions of 2005 thereby 
delaying the laying of the notifications by one year.  Even in cases where there has 
been a delay of 6 -7 months, the Ministry could have laid the notifications during 
the Winter Session-2005.  The Committee is not satisfied with the reasons given by 
the Ministry for the delay and expects them to be prompt and vigilant in the laying 
of subordinate legislation within the stipulated period as recommended in its 131st 
Report (relevant extracts reproduced in para 3 of the report).   The Committee 
hopes that the Ministry will evolve some systematic procedure to avoid such 
instances in future. 
  
  
(viii)       Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways  
(Department of Road Transport & Highways) 
  
The Committee regrets to note that out of a total of 204 Notifications laid 
by the Department of Road Transport & Highways of the Ministry of Shipping, 
Road Transport & Highways, there has been a delay in the laying of 16 
notifications (Sl No. 336-341, 354-361, 374-375.  The delay ranges from 3½ months 
(Sl No. 355-361), 5 months (Sl No. 354 and 376), 8 months (Sl No. 341), 11 months 
(Sl No. 338-340), 1 year ( Sl No. 374 and 375), 2 years (Sl No. 337)  and 3 years (Sl 
No. 336).  A delay statement has been appended with all the notifications which  
states, “It took time to collect the papers and complete the procedural 
formalities.  As such the notifications could not be laid on the Table of both Houses 
of Parliament during the last session.”   The Committee expects the Ministry of 
Shipping, Road Transport & Highways to exercise caution in the matter of timely 
laying of subordinate legislation and ensure that the schedule prescribed by it in 
this behalf is followed meticulously.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to 
evolve some systematic procedure to avoid such instances in future. 
  
3.         The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take 
immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. The 
Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice o f all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131 st,135th  and 152 nd 
Reports: 
            “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House 
is not in Session, during the Session immediately following the date of publication 
of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date 
of the publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time l ag 
between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less 
than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said 
Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under 
various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
(131st Report) 

            “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in 
case there is a dela y in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concerned 
Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The 
Committee desires all Ministries/Departments t o take a note of this, since the 
intension is that through the process of formulation of a delay statement the 
Ministry is able to introspect, identifying bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135th Report) 
            “In the opinion of the Committe e, every notification should be assigned a 
distinctive number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no 
notification should be published/laid which does not carry a notification number. 
The Committee expects all Ministries/Departments of Go vernment of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where there are more than one notification 
under a single file, the Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file number 
on each notification should be suitably distinguished from one another. 
(152nd Report)

.

1.3       The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc.  were laid on 
the Table of the Rajya Sabha during its 208th session  (July-August, 2006) 
have been perused by the Committee in the light of the provisions of the

whether these have been laid properly and  within the prescribed time-
frame.  The Committee’s observations/recommendations are contained in 
the report that follows.

I        Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of Rajya Sabha 
   
            During the 208th Session of the Rajya Sabha, (24th July to 25th 
August,2006) 415 Statutory  Orders were laid on the Table of the House 
by various Ministries/Departments. The details of the Gazette 
Notifications in which these were published and the date of their laying on 
the Table of the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise 
statement placed at Annexure. Out of the above notifications that were 
laid, there has been delay in laying of some of the  notifications as per the 
details given below :-
