file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/169threport.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:52]
            SIDBI Pension Regulations, 1993 were not notified and, therefore, SIDBI Pension Regulations, 2002, notified in 2002
were not in supersession of SIDBI Pension Regulations, 1993. It has been incorrectly stated in the title of the notification that
these had been issued in supersession of the SIDBI Pension Regulations, 1993. The action will be initiated to amend the title of
the SIDBI Pension Regulations, 2002.
Committee's Observation (27.04.04):-
 
            The Ministry have admitted that the Committee had been wrongly informed that the regulations had been issued in
supersession of the SIDBI Pension Regulations, 1993. The Ministry promised to rectify the position.
 
            Action Taken by the Ministry (10.06.04):-
 
            We propose to amend the title to the Pension Regulations, 2002 suitably by a Notification, which would be published in
the Official Gazette after getting approval of the Board of Directors of SIDBI. A copy of the amendment would be forwarded in
due course.
 
            Committee’s further Observations (22.02.05):-
 
            The Ministry have stated that the Small Industries Development Bank of India Pension Regulations, 1993 were not
notified. The Committee desired to know the justification for not notifying the said regulations.
 
            Ministry’s further Comments (13.06.05):-
 
            SIDBI was created out of IDBI w.e.f. April 02, 1990 as per SIDBI Act, 1989. Since its formation, SIDBI is following the
service regulations and all other rules relating to the service matters as that of IDBI. IDBI Pension Regulations were notified in
1995 and have been made applicable w.e.f. November 01, 1993. In terms of the sixth bi-partie settlement between the IBA and
the unions/associations of the bank employees, the pension scheme was introduced in the nationalized banks w.e.f. November
01, 1993, but notified in 1995. SIDBI also formulated the Pension Regulations in 1993 in anticipation of approval of the
Government. During the course of the consideration of the pension regulations, the question of constituting Pension Fund had
arisen and it was considered that since SIDBI had been granted tax exemption, there may not be any need of constituting a
separate Pension Fund. On further consideration of the matter, it was felt to explore the possibility of adopting the pattern of
RBI & NABARD Employee Gratuity and Superannuation Fund Regulations instead of having a separate Pension Regulations in
line with IDBI, which had become a tax paying corporate entity. It, therefore, necessitated an exercise afresh to draft the SIDBI
Employee Gratuity and Superannuation Fund Regulations in line with RBI Regulations. Due to the above development and
subsequent developments like divestment of shares of IDBI in SIDBI and other allied developments, the Pension Regulations of
SIDBI were revisited and SIDBI Pension Regulations, 2002 were notified. It may be pertinent to mention that due to the late
notification of the SIDBI Pension Regulations, the employees have not been affected in any manner as the said Pension
Regulations cover employees from the date of creation of SIDBI subject to fulfillment of conditions.

work exceeding thirteen hours per week and who opts and is governed by these regulations, but shall not include a person
employed either on contract basis or on daily wages;

the Bank for the purpose of pension?
Ministry Reply (01.07.03):-
 
            SIDBI was established as a subsidiary of IDBI under SIDBI Act, 1989 and came into being w.e.f. 2.4.90. As Section
33(2) of SIDBI Act, the employees taken on deputation from IDBI would be governed by the same terms and conditions of
service as were applicable to them in IDBI. Accordingly, the definition of employee has been adopted from the definition of
employee in IDBI Service Regulations.
           
            Now, after delinking of SIDBI from IDBI vide notification dated 10.10.2001, the matter would be reviewed in the light
of observations of the Committee.
 
            Committee's Observation (27.04.04):-
 
            The Ministry agreed to the Committee's suggestion for amending definition of 'employee'.

(vi)              On the issue raised vide point no 10, by proposing to make necessary changes in the numbering of the regulations.
The Committee had pointed out the discrepancy in the numbering of the regulations and had suggested correction
therein for the sake of uniformity.
 
            The Committee is, however, unhappy to note the shift in the Ministry’s stand from time to time while corresponding
with its on various points in the questionnaire like point nos. 1, 2, 3, and 6, to mention a few. While the Committee agrees to
some extent to the Government’s logic to keep in line with the Pension Regulations of other financial institutions, but in that
case they should not act as an obstacle and retard the evolution in similar legislation that is taking place in other
institutions/organizations of Government.   For example, inclusion of part time workers within the definition of the term
‘employee’, Regulation 2(7) does not go well with the present time.   In Committee’s view, SIDBI is a statutory body and it
should have an effective and efficient set of subordinate legislations to enable it to discharge its obligations responsibly, and it
should not feel constrained on any account, including the keeping of parity with other financial institutions, in this endeavour of
theirs.  The Committee, accordingly, recommends the Ministry to review the regulations in the light of the Committee
suggestions that have been put forth during the course of its deliberations, keeping aside all constraints that have been pointed
out so that Regulations are efficient and relevant to the current times.

2.         During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted some cases where there has been a considerable time lag
between the date of notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in cases
where notifications have not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by the Committee and where such notifications were accompanied
by a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has been quite long. The
observations/recommendations of the Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: -  
           
(i) Ministry of Civil Aviation
 
            The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of up to eleven months on the part of the Ministry of Civil Aviation in
laying three of their notifications (Sl. Nos 2,3,& 4) and  in all the cases the Ministry have not appended the delay statements .
           
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Civil Aviation would avoid delay in laying of the notifications and in case of any delay
actually taking place in laying , a delay statement is invariably appended.
 
 
(ii) Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion)
 
           
 
      The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion) have
delayed by three months the laying of their notification (Sl. No. 6).  The Ministry have not appended any delay statement even with the
said notification. The Committee hopes that the Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion shall take necessary steps to ensure that
such delay does not recur and in case it is there then the Parliament is kept informed of the reasons therefor through delay statement.
 
(iii)       Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department of Telecommunication)
 
            The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department of
Telecommunication) have delayed the laying of one of their notification (Sl. 15) by seven months.  The Ministry have appended delay
statement with the notification and the reasons given by the Ministry read thus:
 
      “ The TRAI had sent the regulations to Department of Telecommunications on 21
st February, 2007, after receiving copies of the
regulations in the TRAI on 29th December, 2004 from Controller of Publication, Government of India, after notification of the regulations
in Govt. of India Gazette.  Accordingly there was a delay in laying the regulations on the Table of the House.”
           
            The Committee regrets to note that TRAI had taken around two months to forward the printed copy of the Regulations to the
Department of Telecommunication. But the latter also did not show promptness and the regulations which were received on 21.02.07 were
laid in the Rajya Sabha on 10.05.07. The Committee hope that Department of Telecommunication would take necessary precaution to
ensure that such an instance is not repeated.
 
(iv)   Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department of Posts)
 
            The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry have delayed   laying of one of their notification (Sl No.17). The delay

            The Committee expects the Ministry of Labour & Employment (Directorate General of Employment& Training) to exercise

Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following
recommendations, as contained in its 131st,135th  and 152nd Reports:
      “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session
immediately following the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in
Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the
date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the
Session immediately following the said Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.
(131st Report)
(Presented on 15 December 2000)
      “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying of
Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the
notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the process of formulation of a
delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”.
(135
th Report)
(Presented on 27 July 2001)
 
      “In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned a distinctive number in order to give it
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be published/laid which does not carry a notification
number. The Committee expects all Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this
regard. In case where there are more than one notification under a single file, the Ministries/Departments should
ensure that the file number on each notification should be suitably distinguished from one another.
(152nd Report)

I
 
The Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998.
 
 
          The Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 framed under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 was examined
and a questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution,
(Directorate of Vanaspati, Vegetable Oils & Fats) on the 29
th September, 1999 for their comments/clarifications thereon.   The
Ministry vide their O.M. dated the 26 th May, 2000 furnished their comments/clarifications on each point raised in the
questionnaire. The points referred to the Ministry and their comments/clarifications thereon are reproduced below: -

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/172%20Report.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:19]
 
1.       Point raised
Whether the Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 has been laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha, if so, the
details in this regard.
Ministry’s Comments
41 copies of the Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 issued vide Notification NO. GSR. 584 (E) dated 17-
09-1998 and Corrigendum No. GSR 702 (E) dated 30-11-1998 alongwith one copy of each in Hindi and in English
authenticated by the Minister (Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution) were sent to both Lok Sabha and Rajya  Sabha
Secretariats on 10-12-1998 vide this Directorate’s letter No. 17/1/98-EXP. dated 09-12-1998. While information from Lok
Sabha regarding laying of the papers on the Table on 15-12-1998 (vide Lok Sabha Bulletin Part –I No. 58) has been received,
the information from Rajya Sabha has not be received so far.
 
2.       Point raised- 
Clause 2(b)
          “Edible Oils” mean  vegetable oils and fats and include any i.e, margarine, vanaspati, bakery shorting and fat spread as
specified in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954) and rules made there under, for human consumption;”
Whether the term “edible oils” include ghee and butter also and if not, the justification for non-inclusion of these items
within the meaning of the term.
Ministry’s Comments
The term “Edible Oils” does not include ghee and butter, as ghee and butter are of animal origin and not of vegetable
origin. The term “edible oils” means vegetable oil as per the definition of “edible oils”
 
3.       Point raised- Clause 2(c)
          “Edible Oils Commissioner” means the person appointed as Edible Oils Commissioner by the Central Government and
includes any other person empowered by the Central Government to exercise any or all of the functions of the Edible Oils
commissioner under this Order;”
Whether there are any qualifications or conditions precedent to empowering any person to exercise any or all the
functions of the Edible Oil Commissioner and if so, whether Government have any objection in prescribing them in the Order
itself.
Ministry’s Comments
No qualification has been explicitly stated. The implicit understanding is that the person empowered to exercise the
functions of the Edible Oils Commissioner would be a Senior Gazetted Officer of the Central/ State Government competent
enough to handle the responsibility of the job assigned and enjoying the confidence of the superiors.
 
Action Taken
Modified the provision of Clause 2 (c) of the Order vide notification dated 22 nd November, 2005 (Annexure VII-
Appendix ‘A’)
 
4.       Point raised- 
Clause 3(b)
          “which is not packed in a container, marked and labeled in the manner as specified in the Scheule-1:
                  Provided that the State Government may, in the public interest, for reasons to be recorded in writing, in specific
circumstances and for a specific period by a notification in the Official Gazette, exempt any edible oil from the provisions of
this Order.”
What is the justification for empowering the State Governments to exempt any edible oil from the provisions of this
Order? What are the specific circumstances in the mind of the Ministry behind prescribing for such exemption? Further, there

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/172%20Report.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:19]
is no provision in the clause under which the State Government is under any obligation to inform the Central Government or
the Edible Oils Commissioner regarding the exemption given to any edible oil. Whether such information is not desirable in the
opinion of Government; what is the reaction of the Ministry in this regard? Whether these provisions are being implemented in
a foolproof manner?
Ministry’s Comments
The Central Government is aware of the fact that the production of edible oils is highly decentralized. Substantial
quantity is produced in the small scale or unorganized sector. Further, a sizeable portion of the population is living below the
poverty line. It is in view of these situations that the State Governments have been empowered to exempt any edible oil from
the provisions of this Order in specific circumstances and for specific period only in the public interest for reasons to be
recorded in writing and for specific period only.
          Further vide 
Clause 15, the Edible Oil Commissioner has been authorized to issue appropriate directions including
seeking of information from the State Governments for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of the Packaging Order.
 
5.       Point raised- Clause 4(1) read with Schedule-III
“Registration: No person shall carry on business as a packer except under a certificate of registration granted to him
under this Order and in accordance with the terms and conditions specified in the Schedule-III.”
One of the terms and conditions for grant of certificate of registration is that the registered packer shall not employ any
person who is suffering from infection/contagious disease which is likely to affect packing in hygienic conditions. Which is the
authority that would determine whether any particular disease is infectious or contagious; whether Government have any
objection in prescribing the competent authority in the Order itself? Further, it has been made obligatory for each registered
packer to maintain a register showing the quantity sold. Is it not possible that a registered packer may not be engaging himself
in selling, the product and that he might be doing only the packaging work, in that case such a registered packer would not be
able to comply with this condition and he would be unable to keep a record of the edible oil sold. Whether Government have
any objection in suitable modification of this condition? 
Ministry’s Comments
The power for implementation of the Packaging Order is delegated to the State Governments. It has been left to the State
Governments to decide as to how they will carry-out the various provisions of the order. We have already written to the State
Governments that in case there is any operational difficulty in the implementation of the Order, these may be brought to the
notice of the Central Government so as to resolve the issue in a manner which is not inconsistent with the provisions of this
Order.
 
6.       Point raised- 
Clause 4(2)
          “Every person who intends to carry on the business of a packer shall make an application to registering authority in the
Form specified in the Schedule-II together with the fee to be paid to the State Government, in such manner as may be specified
by the State Government.”
The provision does not specify the quantum of fee to be paid to the State Government along with the application form to
the registering authority. What is the justification for not prescribing the quantum of fees and the manner in which it could be
paid?
Ministry’s Comments
          As already indicated, the power for implementation of the Packaging Order has been delegated to the State Government.
It has been left to the State Government to specify the quantum of fee having regard to the local situations etc.
 
7.       Point raised- Clause 4(3)
“No person shall be eligible for grant of certificate of registration under this Order unless he has his own laboratory

facilities and has appointed in that laboratory at least one chemist having Bachelor of Science Degree with Chemistry as one
of the subjects or has made any other arrangement of a common laboratory for such purpose to the satisfaction of the
registering authority for testing of samples of edible oils.”
The words “to the satisfaction of the registering authority” appearing in the above Order seem to be unwarranted as they
tend to give an unwanted discretion to the registering authority. Once a condition has been prescribed in the order, the same has
to be implemented by the registering authority and making the things subject to satisfaction of an authority seems to be
redundant. What is the opinion of the Ministry in this regard and whether they have any objection in suitable modification of
the provision?
Ministry’s Comments
          We would like the State Governments to start implementation of the Packaging Order. In case, there is any operational
difficulty in the course of implementation of the packaging Order, Central Government will definitely consider suitable
modifications of the provisions of the order.
 
8.       Point raised- Clause 4(4)
“After making necessary enquiries, the registering authority may, as he deems fit, issue certificate of registration
containing terms and conditions to the applicant as specified in Schedule-III or reject the application, for reasons to be
recorded in writing, within ninety days from the date of receipt of application:”
As per the provisions, the registering authority has been allowed 90 days time for the disposal of an application. This
period appears to be too long. Whether Government have any objection in reducing this period to 60 days?
Ministry’s Comments
As replied under question No. 7 above.
Action Taken
          The Ministry has reduced the number of days for the disposal of an application under the section from 90 days to 60 days
vide notification dated the 16th June, 2004.
 
9.       Point raised- Clause 4(5)
“Where a certificate of registration is not granted to a person under this clause, the fee paid by him shall be refunded to
him in the manner as specified by the State Government.”
The Order does not specify the amount of fee to be deposited along with the application and Clause 4(5) states that the
individual shall be refunded the fee paid by him where a certificate of registration is not granted. If the fee is charged only to
offset cost of administrative work involved in the processing of papers, there is no justification for prescribing for its refund in
case of non-issue of the certificate. But, in case, the quantum of fee being charged is on the higher side, with the objective of
keeping a check on the unnecessary and frivolous applications, the so called “fee” deserves to be split up in two parts; one
being the cost of the services involved and the other as security money and the refund of the security money is justified in case
of non-issue of certificate. In such a case, the quantum of security money can well be prescribed in the Order itself. What is the
reaction of the Ministry towards this?
Ministry’s Comments
Same as replied under Question No. 5.
 
10.     Point raised- Clause 5(4)
“Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-clauses (1) and (2), the Edible Oils Commissioner may by order published
in the Official Gazette, specify any other conditions to be complied with by a registered packer, and it shall be the duty of every
registered packer to comply with such conditions.”
As per the provisions, there has been a further delegation of powers upon the Edible Oils Commissioner with regard to

prescribing other conditions to be complied with by a registered packer. What is the justification for delegating such powers on
the Edible Oils Commissioner when such conditions have been prescribed in the Order itself? Should the powers delegated not
be exercised by the Central Government only?
Ministry’s Comments
It is not possible to foresee all the situations during implementation of the Packaging Order. Delegation of such power to
the Edible Oils Commissioner has been considered necessary so as to take care of emergent situations. Edible Oils
Commissioner, it may be mentioned, is the representative of the Central Government and cannot exercise the powers in his
individual capacity.
 
11.     Point raised- Clause 7(1)
“Renewal of certificate of registration(1) Every registered packer shall make an application for renewal of registration
within the period of sixty days before the date of expiry of the certificate of registration to the registering authority in the form
specified in the Schedule-II together with the fee specified by the State Government to be paid to the registering authority in the
manner as may be specified by the State Government for such renewal.”
What is the justification for charging fee at the time of making an application for renewal of certificate for registration?
Here again, the Order does not specify the quantum of fees prescribed to be charged for the purpose.
Ministry’s Comments
Same as replied under Question No. 5
 
12.     Point raised- Clause 7(3)
“Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-clauses (1) and (2), the certificate of registration issued or renewed under
this Order shall be valid till a decision on the application for its renewal is taken by the registering authority.”
As per the provisions, certificate of registration issued or renewed remains valid till a decision on the application for its
renewal is final. Such provision leaves scope for misuse of powers and the registered packer might take undue advantage due
to prolonging of the decision on his application for renewal. Whether Government have any objection in prescribing a time

Act 17 of 1982 with effect from 31.5.1982.
Committee’s observation

laying provision in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 prior to 1982.  The Committee desired that the regulations should
be laid now alongwith the amendments suggested by it.

Ministry’s reply
          Section 124 (1) of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 provides that no regulation made by the Board under the Act
(other than a regulation made under sub-section 2 of section 17) shall have effect until it has been approved by the

regulation is accordingly worded for the regulations to come into effect from date of publication of Government’s

are reproduced below: -    
 
1.       Point raised
Rule 5: Vacancies
“The Board may, in consultation with its Sponsor Bank, determine the number of vacancies in each category of
posts to be filled keeping in view, the guidelines issued by Central Government from time to time.”
(i)                What are the present Guidelines of the Central Government in this regard?
(ii)              Whether Board of Rural Banks have ever reviewed the guidelines issued by the Central Government for
determining the number of vacancies in each category of the posts?
Ministry’s reply
The Central Government has issued the norms and guidelines for creation and filling of the vacancies in various
cadres and appointments and promotion to the newly created posts from time to time.   Recently, the Government of
India has constituted a Working Group to review the staffing norm in RRBs.  The Working Group is likely to submit
its report shortly.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee felt that RRBs should give some autonomy for recruitment of staff.  The Committee noted that
the recruitment was temporarily banned in order to re-adjust the surplus staff and that the surplus staff could be
redeployed from one bank to another.   The Committee further noted that RRBs could also hire people on contract
basis, if required.
 
 
Action taken 
In terms of Government of India letter No.7 (5)/2004-RRB dated 2.11.2004, (Annexure-I)  freedom has been
given to the sponsor banks to recuit/redeploy RRB staff as per their requirement keeping in view the financial health of
the concerned RRB, its existing management costs, besides the business potential of the RRB and suitability of the
staff to be redeployed/recruited for realizing that potential.   These instructions were reiterated vide letter No.7
(5)/2004-RRB dated 4.8.2005 (Annexure-II) .  Accordingly, the sponsor banks are required to re-assess the manpower
requirement and to fill up the posts.
 
2.       Point raised
Rule 10(1)  Recruitment to the posts of messenger, messenger-cum-sweeper, driver, driver-cum-messenger
and security guard-
“The posts of messenger, messenger-cum-sweeper, driver, driver-cum-messenger and security guard shall be
filled in by the Committee of the Regional Rural Banks after making a reference to the Employment Exchange, Sainik
Board or other agencies catering to the welfare of Schedule castes/Scheduled tribes, physically handicapped persons
or other categories of persons as are recognized by the Central Government or the State Government having

jurisdiction over the Regional Rural Bank filling the posts.”
What are the other agencies to which reference is made for filling up of vacancies?   In what manner the
recommendations of Employment Exchange or other agencies are given effect to; whether the candidates
recommended by Employment Exchange and other agencies are given equal weight age?
Ministry’s reply
The reserved vacancies in the Group ‘C’ are required to be filled up in the RRBs as per the procedure indicated
in Chapter 7 of the Brochure on reservation for SC/ST – (8th edition) which are as under:
i)                   All the vacancies should be notified to the local/regional Employment Exchange.
ii)                 When a local Employment Exchange is unable to nominate any suitable candidate, it will refer vacancies to the
Central Employment Exchange.
iii)
               If sufficient numbers of SC/ST candidates are not available through Employment Exchange the vacancies
should be advertised in local newspapers.
iv)
               Simultaneously, with the advertisement, the vacancies should be brought to the notice of the SC/ST
organisations listed in Appendix 11 to be said Brochure.  While doing so, it should be made clear to such organisations
that their function is limited to advising the SC/ST candidates about the recruitment proposed and that it will not be for
them to recommend or press the names of any individuals.   The candidates should apply to the appointing authority
either direct or through the Employment Exchange as the case may be.
As against the above instructions, Rule 10 indicates that the reference is required to be made out to the Other
Agencies also in addition to the Employment Exchange and the Jila Sainik Board.  Further, the second proviso to the
said rule also states that no candidate other than those sponsored by the Employment Exchange, Sainik Board or Other
Agencies shall be called for interview.  However, it can be observed from the above that the other agencies are merely
informed, when the required numbers of candidates are not available through Employment Exchange/Sainik Board and
these agencies do not have powers to sponsor the name of the candidates.  In view of the above, Rule 10 is slightly at
variance with the above guidelines in the Brochure.  Accordingly, the Government will consider amending Rule 10 in
consultation with the Ministry of Law.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee desired that the procedure as laid down in Rule 10(1) needs to be realigned so as to resolve the
ambiguities as pointed out by it.  The Committee impressed upon the need to modify the provisions of Rule 10(1).
Action taken
The necessary amendments in Rule 10(1) were carried out vide  notification dated 16.10.2002 (Annexure-III) . 
The observations of the Committee therefore stand complied with.

Ministry have any objection in incorporating the same in the rule itself?
Ministry’s reply
The Government have no objection to incorporate OBCs in the proviso to rule 10(1).
Committee’s Observation
The Committee noted that the Ministry had no objection in including the OBC candidate also, along with the
SC/ST candidates, for being given preference under proviso to Rule 10(1).
Action taken

4.       Point raised
Schedule-III
Against the eligibility column for various posts covered in the schedule, a minimum period of service has been
prescribed which the officer should have rendered before he is eligible to be considered for promotion to the next
higher scale.  In the same breath, there is a proviso for relaxation in the qualifying service for a period up to 2 years,
in case eligible officers are not available.
Normally, the Rule lays down the eligibility criteria only and in case any relaxation is called for, the powers are
exercised under a general clause in the Rule providing the Competent Authority with the powers to relax in certain
cases.  The pattern followed in the Third Schedule i.e. providing for relaxation in the qualifying service in case of each
of the post separately is a deviation from the normal procedure more particularly because the power to relax in the
Rules is exercisable only in extreme cases of hardship and for removal of disability, is any.  On the other hand, in the
present case, the power to relax the condition of length of service has been made to form a part of the eligibility
criteria thereby giving an impression that the eligibility condition can be relaxed in a routine manner in case eligible
persons are not available.
What is the justification for adopting a changed pattern in the rules in hand and whether Government have any
objection in recasting the provisions in the changed pattern?
Ministry’s reply
The Rule specifically lays down a criterion, which stipulates that relaxation is to be made only if eligible officers
are not available.  This relaxation can be made only with the prior approval of the National Bank who will ensure that
this is not done in a routine manner.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee noted the clarification given by the Ministry during the course of discussions that relaxations are
not made in a routine manner.  The Committee, however, felt that the circumstances for allowing relaxation should
really deserve and that it should be on a case-to-case basis and that the reasons for the same should be required to be
recorded.  The Ministry agreed to the Committee’s suggestions.
Action taken
While allowing relaxations, NABARD ensures on a case by case basis that there are no other eligible officers
available and that all the criteria prescribed for allowing relaxation are satisfied.

It is felt that presence of a Member from these communities in the Committee is essential more particularly
when any official from these categories is to be considered by the Committee. Whether Government have any
objection in substituting the word “may” by the word “shall”?
Ministry’s reply
The word “may” used in the relevant rule has the connotation of “shall”.   The Committee constituted under this
rule invariably comprises of members belonging to SC/STs.
Committee’s Observation

additional member of the Board.

The Government of India vide notification dated 13.07.2004 (Annexure-IV) has substituted the word “may” with

6.       Point raised
Schedule-III
For appointment to the posts in the Schedule, the method of promotion has been stated to be on the basis of
seniority-cum-merit.
What are the main features of this procedure for promotion; Whether it is permissible to change the seniority of
officials as it exists in the feeder grade while recommending their names for promotion to the next higher grade which
is inherent in the “selection” as a method of promotion at least for the purpose of promotion in scale III, scale II and
scale I so as to promote merit in the organisation?
Ministry’s reply
“Seniority-cum-merit” shall mean seniority and found fit for promotion.   It is not possible to change the
seniority of officials, as it exists in the feeder grade.  Thus, seniority-cum-merit implies promotions based on seniority
subject to minimum necessary merit requisite for the promotion.  The Government feels that there should be a uniform
criterion for promotion to all scales and that the present system may continue.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee came across divergent views on the point of promotion on the basis of seniority-cum-merit.  The
Bank of Rajasthan was of the view that promotion should not be purely on the basis of seniority only and merit should
also be given at least 50% weight age.  The Dungarpur Banswara Gramin Bank was of the view that in lower scales,
weight age may be given to seniority but in higher scale merit should prevail.   The Gramin Bank was of the view that
promotion should be made on the basis of both seniority and merit.  The Committee reiterated the need for balance
between seniority and merit to keep the Regional Rural Banks competitive with the other commercial banks.
Action taken
The existing recruitment rules provide for filling up the posts by seniority-cum-merit.   It, therefore, gives due
weightage to the seniority as well as merit.    However, the position would be reviewed after the process for
amalgamation is completed.

“The issue has been re-examined and it may be pointed out that the system of approval of fish and fishery
products establishments has been changed in line with the new EC Regulation No: 854/2004.  Accordingly, new

the initial approval the establishment would be assessed by the Inter-Departmental Panel (IDP) at two stages.  During
the first visit, the IDP would assess the infrastructural facilities of the establishment as well as the compliance to the
regulatory requirements specified in the Government of India notification.   If satisfied, the IDP would recommend for
the ‘conditional approval’ of the establishment.   The conditional approval would be granted by the Competent
Authority for a period of 3 months, which would be extended to a maximum period of 6 months.  During the

would recommend for the ‘full approval’ of the establishment.
 
     Therefore, as the process of granting full approval to the establishment may take considerable time, which may vary
from less than one month to six months, it is not practical to fix any time limit for grant of approval in the Rules.

notification.  However, in such case, where the importing country requires additional parameters to be certified, it

(a)     Merit, suitability and seniority in cases of Class I and II posts:

'merit' and seniority are the words that are used; what is the justification for deviations from general

Ministry’s Comments
:- (14/03/2002)
          IRDA has reported that word "suitability" has been included deliberately in the regulations as a
situation may so arise that a person in spite of being meritorious and senior in a particular cadre may not be

whereby the Chairperson has to make specific recommendation and take approval of the Authority, which
comprises of both full-time and part-time members. If officers having the prescribed qualifying service are
available, their cases will undoubtedly by considered by the Authority.

Government orders on reservations for the reserved category persons and allow to them suitable relaxation
in age, educational qualification, experience, etc. The Committee recommends that the policy decision of
IRDA should find a clear mention in their Regulation, so that the policy gets a statutory recognition. As
regard to the autonomy conferred upon IRDA in the matter of recruitment and promotion, the Committee
feel that the justification given for the autonomy may no doubt sound appealing, but vesting of wide 
discretion  in any authority is always liable to be misused.
 
While the Committee appreciates the need for autonomy as projected by the IRDA, but in the
Committee’s view, subordinate legislation in the form of Rules/ Regulations should be codified to the
optimum, particularly when they are to regulate the recruitment/promotion policy of an organization which
has a bearing on its manpower. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that IRDA may review their
regulations to see to what extent they can do away with the element of subjectivity, of course without
compromising with their efficiency standards.

          The Small Industries Development Bank of India Pension Regulations, 2002 framed under the Small

1)      Point Raised:-
 
          The regulations under examination are in supersession of the pension regulations of 1993. What are

          SIDBI Pension Regulations, 1993 were not notified and, therefore, SIDBI Pension Regulations, 2002,

          The Ministry have admitted that the Committee had been wrongly informed that the regulations had

          Action Taken by the Ministry (10.06.04):-

file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/173th%20Report.htm[25-10-2016 16:41:51]
 
          We propose to amend the title to the Pension Regulations, 2002 suitably by a Notification, which
would be published in the Official Gazette after getting approval of the Board of Directors of SIDBI. A
copy of the amendment would be forwarded in due course.
 
          Committee’s further Observations (22.02.05):-
 
          The Ministry have stated that the Small Industries Development Bank of India Pension Regulations,
1993 were not notified. The Committee desired to know the justification for not notifying the said
regulations.
 
          Ministry’s further Comments (13.06.05):-
 
          SIDBI was created out of IDBI w.e.f. April 02, 1990 as per SIDBI Act, 1989. Since its formation,
SIDBI is following the service regulations and all other rules relating to the service matters as that of IDBI.
IDBI Pension Regulations were notified in 1995 and have been made applicable w.e.f. November 01, 1993.
In terms of the sixth bi-partie settlement between the IBA and the unions/associations of the bank
employees, the pension scheme was introduced in the nationalized banks w.e.f. November 01, 1993, but
notified in 1995. SIDBI also formulated the Pension Regulations in 1993 in anticipation of approval of the
Government. During the course of the consideration of the pension regulations, the question of constituting
Pension Fund had arisen and it was considered that since SIDBI had been granted tax exemption, there may
not be any need of constituting a separate Pension Fund. On further consideration of the matter, it was felt
to explore the possibility of adopting the pattern of RBI & NABARD Employee Gratuity and
Superannuation Fund Regulations instead of having a separate Pension Regulations in line with IDBI,
which had become a tax paying corporate entity. It, therefore, necessitated an exercise afresh to draft the
SIDBI Employee Gratuity and Superannuation Fund Regulations in line with RBI Regulations. Due to the
above development and subsequent developments like divestment of shares of IDBI in SIDBI and other
allied developments, the Pension Regulations of SIDBI were revisited and SIDBI Pension Regulations,
2002 were notified. It may be pertinent to mention that due to the late notification of the SIDBI Pension
Regulations, the employees have not been affected in any manner as the said Pension Regulations cover
employees from the date of creation of SIDBI subject to fulfillment of conditions.

      The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 2005  
 
 The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 
2005 framed under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 were 
examined and certain points, which needed further 
comments/clarifications, were put together in the form of a questionnaire. 
It was forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs for their 
comments/clarifications on July 10, 2006.  In reply, the Ministry of Home 
Affairs vide their communication dated October 16, 2006 informed as 
follows :- 
“….that the comments of Rajya Sabha Secretariat 
were examined and draft   comments were sent to the 
Ministry of Law for vetting.  The Ministry of Law has 
accepted the comments of Ministry of Home Affairs in Rule 
6.  The Comments in Rule 3, 5(1), 5(2), 7(1) and 7(2) have 
been reexamined and fresh comments of this Ministry are 
enclosed. 
 
On receipt of the Rajya Sabha acceptance on the 
proposed comments/amendments, the approval of Hon’ble 
Home Minister will be obtained for notifying the same.” 
 
2. The   points   referred to the Ministry and their comments thereon 
are reproduced below : 
 
1.     Point raised:  Rule 3 : Appointment of Authorised Officer  
“Where the person against whom an order of forfeiture has been 
made (hereinafter referred to as the person), is acquitted, the property 
shall  be returned to him or his legal nominee and if it is not possible for 
any reason to return the forfeited property, the State Government shall 

appoint an officer not below the rank of Deputy Secretary to that 
Government, to be known as Authorised Officer, to evaluate and fix the 
price of the forfeited property with a view to compensating the person in 
lieu of the forfeited property.” 
As per Rule 3, all what has been said about the Authorised Officer 
is that he must not be below the rank of Deputy Secretary of the 
Government. As the job of evaluation is technical, should the Authorised 
Officer not possess some technical qualification also? 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 
In order to have a more cogent procedure for the authorized officer 
to compute the value of forfeited property, it is proposed that Rule 3 
may be amended by inserting an explanation which will allow the 
Authorized Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property. 
 
2.    Point raised: Rule 5 : Consideration of the representation : 
          "(1) The Authorised Officer shall take into account, representation, 
if any, made by the person or his leg al nominee before the final 
determination of the price with respect to the forfeited property is made" 
 Whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time frame 
for disposal of representation, if any, given by the person or his legal 
nominee or f or that matter for completing the whole process of 
determining the price of the forfeited property under the rules? 
 
Ministry's reply 

 180 days from the first day of the next month of the receipt of the 
representation. 
 
3.    Point raised: Rule 5: Consideration of the representation: 
 
          "(2) The Authorised Officer shall thereafter fix the price of the 
forfeited property and intimate the same in writing to the person or his 
legal nominee". 
 Rule 5 mentions that the Authorised Officer shall intimate the person 
or his legal nominee as to the fixing of the price of the forfeited property. 
Rule 6 maintains that the State Government should issue an order to the 
effect that the property stands sold to the State Government at the price 
fixed under rule 5. 
        Whether the intimation to the person/legal nominee is accompanied 
by such an order, or such an arrangement is being viewed as an assurance 
to the concerned individual. 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 60 days from the date the proces s of determining the price of 
forfeited property is completed. 
 The persons/legal nominee is informed about the price of the forfeited 
property as per Rule 5(2) of the said Act. Further reference by the State 
Government to the Central Government about the Head of Account etc. 
is an administrative function only.  The M/o Law and Justice have opined 
that this appears to be sustainable. 
 
4.    Point raised : Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 

           " (1) The Central Government shall on receipt of the order under 
rule 6, deposit the price fixed for the forfeited property in such Treasury 
or under such Head of Account as may be specified therein under 
intimation to the person or his legal nominee." 
 As the matter being of utmost urgency  to the affected individual, 
whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time -frame 
within which the Central Government, after receipt of such an order as 
specified in rule 6, deposit the forfeited property in such Treasury under 
such Head of A ccount as specified in such an order under intimation to 
the person or his legal nominee.   
 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 30 days from the date of order as specified in Rule 6. 
 
5.    Point raised: Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 
           " (2) The amount of price along with interest there on, shall be paid 
to the person  
Or to his legal nominee."  
   
           Sub-rule (2) of Rule 7 mentioned about payment of the price of the 
forfeited property along with "interest thereon". Wheth er Ministry will 
specify at what rate interest will be paid to the claimant? 
 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 

 It is proposed that the interest may be paid at the prevailing interest 
rates on savings bank account of State Bank of India.  
 
The Committee considered the replies of the Ministry of Home 
Affairs on the points forwarded to them.  The Committee notes with 
satisfaction that the Ministry of Home Affairs have agreed to take action 
as follows in pursuance to its suggestions : 
(i) In Rule 3, to insert  an explanation allowing  the Authorized 
Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property.  In the existing rules, 
the Authorised Officer is required to do this job  without any  
assistance; and   
(ii) In Rule  7 (2), to  make provision for paying  the interest at 
the prevailing interest rates on savings bank account of State 
Bank of India on the price of the forfeited property to the 
claimant.  The existing provisions do no mention about  the 
rate of interest. 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry would carry out the above 
amendments expeditiously under intimation to it. However, on other 
points, the Committee notes with satisfaction the reply given by  the 
Ministry of Home Affairs. 
      The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 2005  
 
 The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 
2005 framed under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 were 
examined and certain points, which needed further  
comments/clarifications, were put together in the form of a questionnaire. 
It was forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs for their 
comments/clarifications on July 10, 2006.  The Ministry of Home vide 

their O.M. No. 1-17014/52/2005-IS.VII dated October 16, 2008 stated that 
the points raised by this Secretariat were examined by that Ministry and 
draft comments  on the same were sent to the Ministry of Law  for vetting.  
The Ministry of Law has accepted the comments of Ministry of Home 
Affairs in Rule 6.  The Ministry of Home Affairs have re -examined  the 
Rule 3, 5(1), 5(2), 7(1) & 7(2) and  furnished their reply on these Rules.  
They had also asked for the acceptance of this Secretariat on the 
proposed comments/amendments and after obtaining the  approval of 
Hon’ble Home Minister for notifying  the same. 
The Committee, in its meeting held on 22 nd November, 2007,  
considered the replies of the Ministry of Home Affairs on the points 
forwarded to them and accepted the Ministry’s proposal for taking action 
with regard to the following points : 
(i) In Rule 3, by inserting  an explanation which will allow  the 
Authorized Officer to utilize the service of 
consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to arrive at the value of forfeited 
property; and  
(ii) In Rule  7 (2), by paying  the interest at the prevailing interest
